  1. Background:

The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery Project (PAMP) supports the implementation of the Government program, the Recovery Focused National Development Plan (RF-NDP) 2023-2027. In January 2024, the GoTG approved and adopted the RF-NDP 2023-2027, i.e., program implementation is currently in its infancy. The RF-NDP aims to consolidate gains in democratic governance, accelerate green economic and social transformation, and build resilience to shocks and crises. It has three major strategic objectives: (1) building household and community resilience to address shocks and crises arising from climate change and economic volatility and to counter the effects of pandemics like COVID-19; (2) consolidating gains and addressing critical development gaps in governance and economic and social transformation; and (3) strengthening accountability, building partnerships and setting up robust and sustainable resource mobilization strategies for effective delivery of development actions and expected outcomes. The RF-NDP is organized across seven pillars.

The proposed PforR focuses on a subset of RF-NDP priority actions related to enhancing domestic resource mobilization and financial reporting, human resources management, and citizen engagement in the education sector. These include the second pillar on Governance Reforms priority actions to “enhance governance and management of civil society organizations” and “professionalize and instill meritocracy, ethical conduct, transparency and accountability in the public service and personnel management” and the third pillar on Macroeconomic Stability and Inclusive Growth priority action to “enhance Public Financial Management (PFM) for macro-fiscal stability and strengthening democracy.”

  1. Objective of The Assignment:

The Government of the Gambia (GoTG), through the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs (MoFEA) has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank, for the financing of the Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery Project (PAMP). Coordination and implementation of the PAMP is being undertaken by the Central Projects Coordination Unit (CPCU) of the MoFEA.

The Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education (MoBSE) and the Ministry of Health (MoH) are the two key service-delivery ministries selected to participate in the PAMP, that has a key objective to support service delivery in these two sectors of education and health.

The Program Development Objective (PDO) of PAMP is to enhance domestic resource mobilization, expenditure and human resource management, and mechanisms for citizen engagement. In turn, these reforms support downstream service delivery in the education and health sectors. The PDO is to be achieved through the delivery of activities measured by disbursement-linked indicators in three Results Areas; which are; Results Area 1: Strengthening Management of Public Revenues and Expenditures; Results Area 2: Strengthening the Public Administration and Results Area 3: Improved Transparency and Citizen Engagement in Service Delivery.

  1. Scope of Work:

Review capacity assessment of the governance (regulatory, institutional, technical, and financial) framework underpinning LECs absence/inability to be established or operate effectively, the concerns, and challenges across both the national and local government levels.

Preparation of a detailed and comprehensive report, including recommendations and implementation plan for the GoTG through the NEMC to establish and operationalize all LECs.

    1. Inception report
    2. Review of documents
    3. Stakeholder mapping
    4. Comprehensive analysis
    5. Stakeholder engagement and consultations
    6. Final report and recommendations

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request

  • Master's degree from a recognized university in Environmental Management, Natural Resource Governance, Public Policy, Public Administration, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a closely related field. Additional professional certifications in institutional capacity assessment, results-based management, or participatory planning are desirable.

PROJET FILETS SOCIAUX ADAPTATIFS ET D’INCLUSION ECONOMIQUE- UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET (UGP)

AVIS A SOLLICITATION DES MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET N°005/ASMI/ MINEPAT/ CTS/PFS-AIE/UGP/2026 DU 16 JUILLET 2026 POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UNE FIRME CHARGEES D’APPUYER L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET FILETS SOCIAUX ADAPTATIFS ET D’INCLUSION ECONOMIQUE DANS L’EVALUATION DES PLANS D’AFFAIRES, DU MONTANT REEL DES BESOINS EN SUBVENTION ET DU CALENDRIER DES DECAISSEMENTS EN FAVEUR DES BENEFICIAIRES RETENUS DU DEUXIEME CYCLE DU CONCOURS DE PLANS D’AFFAIRES

 

IDA Crédit N° 70480-CM 

 

Pays : Cameroun

Projet : Projet Filets Sociaux Adaptatifs et d’Inclusion Economique

Crédit IDA : N°70480 CM

 

 

Titre : Recrutement d’une firme chargée d’appuyer l’Unité de Gestion du Projet Filets Sociaux Adaptatifs et d’Inclusion Economique (PFS-AIE) dans l’évaluation des plans d’affaires, du montant réel des besoins en subvention et du calendrier des décaissements en faveur des bénéficiaires retenus du deuxième cycle du Concours de plans d’affaires

 

  1. Contexte et justification

 

Dans sa Stratégie Nationale de Développement 2020-2030 (SND-30) pour la transformation structurelle et le développement inclusif, le Gouvernement s’est engagé à consolider les acquis de la protection sociale et élargir son champ au plus grand nombre de Camerounais, en intégrant progressivement l’ensemble des catégories sociales jusqu’ici en marge du système, à travers la réduction des inégalités sociales, les mesures de protection contre toutes les formes de vulnérabilité, la cohésion et l’inclusion sociales. Pour atteindre ces objectifs, il a articulé ses interventions autour : (i) de la sécurité sociale, (ii) des transferts sociaux et (iii) de l’action sociale.

Dans ce cadre, le Gouvernement a poursuivi la mise en œuvre du Projet Filets Sociaux (PFS) jusqu’en décembre 2022. Le PFS constitue l’un des instruments phares de l’assistance sociale au Cameroun car les filets sociaux accordent des transferts monétaires ciblés aux ménages les plus pauvres. Lancé en 2013 auprès de 2.000 ménages bénéficiaires, le PFS a touché 375 500 ménages en 2022 soit environ 2.000.000 d’individus. Une évaluation du Projet a montré les impacts positifs de grande envergure des transferts monétaires sur les bénéficiaires et dans la communauté. Les filets sociaux ont des effets positifs à court terme et un impact positif à moyen terme sur les bénéficiaires et ils permettent au Gouvernement d’atteindre son objectif de réduction de la pauvreté.

Pour assurer la pérennisation des activités d’un tel Projet, le Gouvernement a mis sur pied, avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale, le Projet Filets Sociaux Adaptatifs et Inclusion Économique (PFS-AIE) qui a pour objectifs d’étendre la couverture et la capacité de la réponse aux chocs du système de filets sociaux aux ménages les plus vulnérables, d’une part et d’accroître l'accès aux opportunités de générer les revenus et de soutenir l'entrepreneuriat chez les jeunes des zones urbaines âgés de 18 à 35 ans, d’autre part.

Le PFS-AIE permettra ainsi : (i) de poursuivre les appuis aux ménages pauvres tels que cela s’est fait dans les trois programmes du PFS, (ii) d’apporter des appuis aux jeunes travailleurs âgés de 18 à 35 ans du secteur informel dans les zones urbaines, (iii) d’apporter des appuis aux jeunes entrepreneurs âgés de 18 à 35 ans ayant des projets d'entreprise prometteurs dans des secteurs productifs ciblés et prioritaires pour le gouvernement, (iv) d’apporter un appui au développement du Registre Social Unifié du Cameroun (RESUC) et (v) de promouvoir le paiement électronique des transferts monétaires aux bénéficiaires du PFS-AIE.

Le PFS-AIE comprend 5 composantes à savoir : (i) Composante 1 « Projet filets sociaux adaptatifs », (ii) Composante 2 « Inclusion économique des jeunes et entrepreneuriat », (iii) Composante 3 « Systèmes numériques de prestation réactifs aux chocs », (iv) Composante 4 « Soutien à la gestion et à la coordination du Projet » et (v) Composante 5 « Composante de réponse d'urgence (CERC) ».

S’agissant de la Composante 2 « Inclusion économique des jeunes et entrepreneuriat », elle vise à soutenir l’emploi décent et à contribuer à la création d'emplois pour les jeunes de 18 à 35 ans à travers deux Sous-composantes : (i) la Sous-composante 2.1, Inclusion économique des jeunes et (ii) la Sous-composante 2.2, Concours des plans d’affaires (CPA).

En ce qui concerne particulièrement la Sous-composante 2.2 « Concours des plans d’affaires », son objectif est de promouvoir des entrepreneurs (âgés de 18 à 35 ans) dans les zones urbaines afin de soutenir le développement de l’entrepreneuriat en mettant l'accent sur les secteurs formel et informel. Il sera notamment question de mener des actions visant à identifier et à soutenir des jeunes entrepreneurs ayant déjà initié une micro, petite et moyenne entreprise (MPME) entre 1 à 3 ans avec un potentiel de croissance significatif et présentant un potentiel de création d'emplois dans les secteurs porteurs et prioritaires pour le gouvernement définis dans la SND-30.

Au total, 2.000 jeunes seront bénéficiaires de cette Sous-composante en 02 phases de 1000 bénéficiaires chacune. Les bénéficiaires recevront en moyenne 5,5 millions FCFA par personne.

Ce concours est ouvert aux jeunes entrepreneurs des zones urbaines, âgés de 18 à 35 ans, opérant dans l'un des secteurs prioritaires du SND30. Les entrepreneurs concourront dans leurs régions d'implantation, les présélectionnés seront formés et des subventions de performance seront attribuées aux bénéficiaires finaux.

Pour la mise en œuvre opérationnelle de cette Sous-composante, les activités suivantes seront réalisées : (i) le lancement & le rodage de la plateforme, (ii) la sensibilisation et la communication, (iii) l’inscription des jeunes et la soumission des notes conceptuelles, (iv) l’apurement des données, (v) la sélection des notes conceptuelles, (vi) la validation et l’enregistrement des présélectionnés, (vii) la formation à travers un bootcamp, (viii) la rédaction des plans d’affaires par les candidats (ix) la soumission en ligne des plans d’affaires, (x) la sélection des bénéficiaires finaux, (xi) l’évaluation des besoins réels et calendrier de décaissement, (xii) la validation et l’enregistrement des bénéficiaires par l’UGP, (xiii) le versement des subventions de performance, (xiv) l’accompagnement technique des bénéficiaires.

2. Objectifs de la mission

 

2.1 Objectif général

 

L’objectif général de la mission du Cabinet est d'appuyer l'Unité de Gestion du PFS-AIE dans l’évaluation des plans d’affaires, du montant réel des besoins en subvention et l’établissement du calendrier des décaissements en faveur de chaque bénéficiaire retenu du deuxième cycle du concours de plans d'affaires.

 

2.2 Objectifs spécifiques

De façon spécifique, il reviendra au prestataire d’assurer :

  1. L’évaluation détaillée de 1500 plans d'affaires soumis par des candidats déjà présélectionnés et formés pour le second cycle du concours ;
  2. Une synthèse générale des notes des 1500 candidats, répartis par ville. La préparation d’une synthèse de maximum deux (2) pages expliquant les forces et faiblesses de chacun des 1500 plans d’affaires à classer dans un dossier pour le jury oral du Concours ;
  3.  L’estimation des besoins réels en subvention pour chacun des 1000 bénéficiaires définitivement sélectionnés après le jury oral ;
  4. Un rapport sur la répartition des subventions par ville et par secteur d’activité ;
  5. La proposition d’un calendrier de décaissement sur la base des différents jalons de mise en œuvre pour chacun des 1000 (mille) bénéficiaires définitivement sélectionnés après le jury oral.

3. Zone de mise en œuvre du cycle 2 du programme CPA

Le cycle 2 du programme des concours de plans d’affaires bénéficiera à 1.000 jeunes entrepreneurs dans les villes de Yaoundé (180 jeunes), Maroua (120 jeunes), Douala (270 jeunes), Garoua (120 jeunes), Bamenda (150 jeunes) et Buea (160 jeunes).

4. Durée de la mission

La durée de la mission est de 6 (six) mois.

5. Profil de la firme d’évaluation

 

La firme doit être un organisme du secteur privé ou un consortium qui œuvre depuis au moins dix ans dans :

  • L’évaluation technique et financière des plans d’affaires des entreprises et projets et l’accompagnement des MPME pour les rendre performantes, innovantes et compétitives ;
  • L’organisation des sessions d’évaluation des projets de création et de développement d’entreprises.

 Enfin, elle doit avoir dans son équipe un chef évaluateur et au moins dix membres évaluateurs ayant les profils suivants :

  • Profil du chef évaluateur
  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme équivalent à BAC+5 minimum dans les filières suivantes : Gestion/Management, Economie, Entrepreneuriat ou tout autre discipline similaire ;
  • Avoir au moins 7 ans d’expérience pertinente dans le domaine de conseil aux entreprises en phase de démarrage ;
  • Avoir une forte expérience cumulée d’au moins 5 ans dans l’accompagnement des jeunes dans la mise en œuvre des activités économiques ;
  • Avoir déjà participé comme évaluateur principal des projets/idées de projet ou business plan depuis au moins sept ans dans un programme de sélection de business plans ;
  • Avoir la capacité de travailler sous pression pour produire et transmettre les rapports de l’exécution technique des activités dans les délais.

       Profil des membres évaluateurs

  • Avoir au moins la maîtrise en gestion, économie, finance, marketing, procédés de fabrication/transformation des produits, ou entreprenariat en fonction de la spécialité ;
  • Au moins 05 ans d'expérience dans le domaine de l’évaluation technique et financière des plans d’affaires et/ou projets de développement des entreprises.

6. Modalités de sélection

Le Cabinet d’évaluation sera sélectionné selon la méthode « Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant » (SQC) en accord avec le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI), Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement, Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants, septième édition, septembre 2025 ».

Les firmes intéressées peuvent obtenir les Termes de Référence et des informations complémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous tous les jours ouvrables entre 8h et 16 heures à l’Unité de Gestion du Projet Filets Sociaux Adaptatifs et d’Inclusion Economique, sis à Yaoundé au quartier Tsinga, Rue 1898, derrière le Palais des Congrès, face Polyclinique du Palais, Email : projetfiletssociaux.aie@gmail.com avec copie à michnjoh@yahoo.fr et  andylobe2000@yahoo.fr,  BP : 5838 Yaoundé-Cameroun.

7. Contenu des manifestations à adresser au PFS-AIE

Le Coordonnateur National du PFS-AIE invite tous les consultants intéressés, à manifester leur intérêt pour la fourniture des services ci-dessus décrits, à produire les éléments suivants :

-    une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée adressée au Coordonnateur National du Projet Filets Sociaux Adaptatifs et d’Inclusion Economique ;

-    une présentation de la firme (justification du statut juridique, principaux domaines d’activités similaires) ;

NB : Toute information pertinente, non justifiée ne sera pas prise en compte.

Les Firmes peuvent s’associer pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives.

Country:        The Republic of the Gambia

Grant Number: IDA-E3820

Project ID NO:  P176924

  1. Background:

The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery Project (PAMP) supports the implementation of the Government program, the Recovery Focused National Development Plan (RF-NDP) 2023-2027. In January 2024, the GoTG approved and adopted the RF-NDP 2023-2027, i.e., program implementation is currently in its infancy. The RF-NDP aims to consolidate gains in democratic governance, accelerate green economic and social transformation, and build resilience to shocks and crises. It has three major strategic objectives: (1) building household and community resilience to address shocks and crises arising from climate change and economic volatility and to counter the effects of pandemics like COVID-19; (2) consolidating gains and addressing critical development gaps in governance and economic and social transformation; and (3) strengthening accountability, building partnerships and setting up robust and sustainable resource mobilization strategies for effective delivery of development actions and expected outcomes. The RF-NDP is organized across seven pillars.

The proposed PforR focuses on a subset of RF-NDP priority actions related to enhancing domestic resource mobilization and financial reporting, human resources management, and citizen engagement in the education sector. These include the second pillar on Governance Reforms priority actions to “enhance governance and management of civil society organizations” and “professionalize and instill meritocracy, ethical conduct, transparency and accountability in the public service and personnel management” and the third pillar on Macroeconomic Stability and Inclusive Growth priority action to “enhance Public Financial Management (PFM) for macro-fiscal stability and strengthening democracy.”

  1. Sectoral Context and Objective of The Assignment:   

Environmental and Social Impact Assessment is a major planning tool being implemented globally and primarily aimed at foretelling the possible negative impacts whilst enhancing the positives and promoting sustainable development. At Rio Earth Summit in 1992, state parties have been enjoined to put in place policy, legislative and institutional framework to ensuring environmental management. Also, state parties have been enjoined in implementing EIA as a planning tool to ensuring sustainable development.

Following through on this international commitment, The Gambia, has in 1992, developed it her premium policy on the environment- the Gambia Environment Action Plan (GEAP), which sought to engender an integrated approach to natural resources management, with a strong emphasis on the need to ensure that environmental considerations are factored in all national plans and projects for sustainability. The NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 PART VII requires the completion of environmental and social screening for all development projects with environmental and social impacts before implementation starts. The objective is to predetermine the extent of potential negative impacts, which in turn determines whether specific projects can be implemented at specific sites.

The EIA Guidelines 1999 and EIA Procedure 1999, are subsidiary instruments aimed at enhancing the requirements of Part V of the Act, as mentioned above, in the implementation of the EIA process in The Gambia. These documents, as the names imply, are guidance tools utilized by both the agency and ESIA consultants to guide the implementation of ESIA process in The Gambia. The tools outlined steps to be followed in screening, scoping, determination of categorization and undertaking of the impact study itself. Together with the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 cited above, these instruments have proven essential to enabling the ESIA processing taking roots in The Gambia since inception in the early 1990s.

  1. Scope of Work:
  1. Scope of Services:
    • Review of the existing instruments – the EIA Procedures (1999) and EIA Guidelines (1999) – to identify gaps.
    • Carry out a literature review of similar instruments implemented in the sub-region and beyond, with a view to identifying and adopting best practices for implementation in The Gambia.
    • Conduct stakeholder engagement to capture valuable suggestions and inputs.
    • Prepare updated instruments: the EIA Procedure and EIA Guidelines.
    • Update the ESIA Guidelines and Procedures, including the screening form.
  1. Key Tasks:
    • Inception report:
    • Review of documents:
    • Stakeholder mapping:
    • Stakeholder engagement and consultations:
    • Updated instruments:
  1. Qualification and Competency
  • A relevant Master's degree (or higher) from a recognized university in Environmental Law, Environmental Management, Environmental Policy, Environmental Science, or a related field.
  • Minimum 12 years of relevant professional experience in environmental assessment, regulatory review, or environmental governance, of which at least 7 years must involve leading assignments of a similar nature, specifically the review or revision of ESIA guidelines, procedures, or equivalent regulatory instruments.
  • At least 2 completed assignments with demonstrable outputs involving the review or development of national EIA/ESIA regulatory frameworks, guidelines, or procedures. Brief descriptions of these assignments, including client, date, and scope, should be provided with the application.
  • Minimum 7 years of experience in stakeholder mapping and participatory consultation, with demonstrated capacity to develop and execute a detailed strategy for engaging NEA, line ministries, the private sector, civil society organizations, and traditional authorities.
  • Proven drafting capacity, with ability to produce ESIA guidelines and procedures that are operationally practical, legally sound, and institutionally feasible for implementation in a public agency context.
  • Familiarity with the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 and relevant Gambian environmental regulations is an advantage. Familiarity with World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (WB ESS) is also an advantage. Candidates are expected to review relevant instruments prior to commencement.
  • Ability to facilitate stakeholder engagement in local Gambian languages (Wolof, Mandinka, Fula, or others) is an advantage. Candidates without this capacity should demonstrate a clear and costed plan for working with qualified interpreters.

Full TOR Availability Notice

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request. Please send your request via email to the addresses provided below. The assignment is expected to be completed within 3 months from the date of signing the contract.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION

Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands

Urban Resilience Project

Grant: IDA-E6610

Assignment: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of a Climate-Resilient Stormwater Drainage System and Stormwater Management Plan for Majuro Atoll

Reference Number: MH-MWIU-558068-CS-QCBS

1. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the RMI Urban Resilience Project (RMIURP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services.

2. The objective of this consultancy is to prepare a comprehensive, climate-resilient Stormwater Drainage System and Stormwater Management Plan for Majuro Atoll through the assessment of the existing drainage network, hydraulic performance, flood risks, asset conditions, and climate change impacts. The assignment will develop a strategic drainage asset management plan, identify priority maintenance, rehabilitation, and capital investment needs, prepare improved drainage design standards and cost estimates, and recommend sustainable maintenance, funding, and institutional arrangements to enhance the long-term resilience, functionality, and management of the stormwater drainage system.

3. The Services will include, among other tasks: (i) preparation of an inception report; (ii) engineering assessments including drainage network mapping; spatial flooding, hydraulic capacity, and condition assessment; sediment sources assessment and control points; wide area drainage assessment; criticality assessment and priority works; improved drainage designs; (iii) public engagement and survey; and (iv) asset management support including maintenance models and requirements, asset condition measures and asset management plan.

4. The complete scope of services and other details pertaining to this assignment, including the key and non-key experts required, are described in the Terms of Reference (TOR) which can be obtained from the email addresses provided below. The expected duration is 15 months under a lump sum contract.

5. The Ministry of Public Works, Infrastructure and Utilities now invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria and scoring are listed in the table below.

No

                             Scoring Criteria

                   Points

   1

General experience of the firm in the past ten (10) years undertaking assignments in drainage studies, hydraulic and hydrology studies, stormwater management assessments, and institutional aspects of stormwater management.

                    20

   2

Demonstrated experience in consultancy assignments of a similar nature to the scope of services defined in the TOR. Relevant specific experiences in stormwater drainage assessment and preparation of stormwater drainage management plans, drainage asset management plan and maintenance. This shall be demonstrated by at least two successfully completed projects in the last ten (10) years.

                     45

   3

Demonstrated experience in consultancy assignments in Pacific countries, atoll environments and/or island environments or other contexts with comparable climate, disaster-risk, land, infrastructure, community consultation and implementation constraints.

                      15

   4

Experience and expertise in consultancy assignments funded by international development agencies, e.g., World Bank, Asian Development Bank, or other similar international financial institutions or funding agencies.

Demonstrated Financial and Managerial Capacity of the Firm.

                    100

6. In addition, the Ministry of Public Works, Infrastructure and Utilities invites interested consultants to provide comments on: The TOR; ways to incorporate social responsibility and Marshallese culture; gender equality of team members; and innovative approaches to the assignment.

7. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Consultants should therefore focus their Expressions of Interest on firm-level qualifications and relevant experience. Key Experts and detailed technical methodology will be evaluated at the Request for Proposals stage.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. The Consultant may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

10. Only shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit technical and financial proposals in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

11. Interested Consultants may obtain further information from the RMIURP Project Manager (contact details below).

12. Expressions of Interest must address the shortlisting requirements indicated above in section 4 (1-6) and section 5 and must not be longer than 30 pages.

13. Expressions of Interest must be delivered to the email addresses given below no later than 14:00hrs (Marshall Islands Time), August 24, 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Country: Ethiopia

Name of Project: Eastern and Southern Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience (EAGER) programme

Grant No: P179293

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant as Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant

Reference No. ET-AUC-561624-CS-INDV

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Eastern and Southern Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience (EAGER) programme and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include maintaining and regularly updating M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records. Specific tasks include:

 

  • Designing and managing databases to store programme data and ensure accurate reporting.
  • Maintaining and regularly updating M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records.
  • Regularly collecting, compiling, analyzing, and synthesizing data and monitoring project progresses against established indicators and targets.
  • Assisting in the administration of surveys, assessments, evaluations, and other data collection activities, including questionnaire preparation, data entry, and initial analysis.
  • Maintaining organized records of M&E documents, reports, datasets, tools, and supporting evidence for audit and reporting purposes.
  • Conducting regular data quality checks and support data verification exercises to ensure completeness, accuracy, consistency, and reliability of reported information
  • Following up with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders on submission of required monitoring data and reporting information, under the guidance of the M&E Officer.
  • Providing regular updates on programme achievements, challenges, and risks to program team and stakeholders
  • Assisting the preparations of monitoring reports, dashboards, data visualizations, and other knowledge products
  • Supporting the preparation of periodic project progress reports, including data summaries, indicator tracking tables, and supporting documentation for governance structures such as the Technical Working Group (TWG), Project Management Team (PMT), and Project Steering Committee (PSC).
  • Supporting the organization of M&E-related meetings, workshops, training sessions, and learning events, including preparation of materials and documentation of proceedings.
  • Supporting the documentation and dissemination of evaluation findings, lessons learned, and good practices.
  • Coordinating routine communication with implementing partners and AU Member States regarding submission of monitoring data and reporting requirements.
  • Supporting the operationalization of the AU Gender and Youth Observatory (AUGYO) through data management, documentation and reporting support.
  • Performing any other related duties assigned by the supervisor.

 

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The African Union Commission now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Social Sciences, International Development, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.
  • Minimum of three years of relevant experience supporting monitoring, evaluation, reporting, or data management functions within development, gender equality, education, or related programmes.
  • Demonstrated experience in data collection, data entry, data management, and preparation of monitoring reports.
  • Experience supporting the use of M&E tools, databases, tracking systems, and data visualization platforms.
  • Basic understanding of results-based management (RBM), monitoring frameworks, indicators, and reporting processes.
  • Knowledge and experience in collecting and managing gender-sensitive data and indicators is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to organize, interpret, and present programme data in a clear and concise manner.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, including experience in preparing reports, summaries, and documentation.
  • Experience working with development partners, government institutions, or international organizations, preferably within the African development context.
  • Proficiency in relevant data management and reporting tools (e.g., Excel, databases, data visualization tools, or other M&E information management systems).
  • Proficiency in English and at least one of the African Union working languages. Good command of French and/or Portuguese is an advantage. 

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 05 August 2026.

 

African Union Commission,

Attn: Head of Supply Chain Management Division

Building C, 3rd Floor,

P.O Box 3243, Roosevelt Street

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Tel: +251 (0) 11 551 7700 – Ext 4305

Fax: +251 (0) 11 551 0442; +251 11-551-0430

E-mails: Tender@AfricanUnion.org

 

 

 

 

 

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

MONITORING AND EVALUATION ASSISTANT FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA GIRLS' EMPOWERMENT AND RESILIENCE (EAGER) PROGRAMME

 

REF: ET-AUC-561624-CS-INDV

  1. Background

 

The African Union Commission (AU) and the World Bank Group have established a strategic partnership and an extensive collaboration in various areas over the past years. Following increased engagement between the Commission and the World Bank, existing collaborations and new programmes on gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) have been established. In 2023, the AUC and World Bank signed an agreement to implement the East and Southern Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience (EAGER) project, to be implemented from 2024 to 2029. The project provides a platform to directly collaborate with AU Member States across Eastern and Southern Africa on women and girls’ empowerment.

 

The EAGER project seeks to increase girls’ and women’s educational attainment and earnings and to strengthen the institutional capacity to implement gender equality policies. The project components include boosting human capital accumulation, enabling access to productive employment, and building the enabling environment to generate change across both formal and informal institutions including development of policies and regulatory frameworks, markets, and social norms that support the adoption of progressive gender equality reforms.

 

  1. Goals and Objectives

 

To maintain and regularly update M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records.

 

  1. Duty Station

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant is expected to be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia at the African Union Headquarters, specifically within the Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD). He/She shall avail time for any travel pertinent to EAGER as requested by the Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD), and/or the Department of Health, Humanitarian Affairs and Social Development (HHSD), and/or the African Union International Centre for Girls and Women’s Education in Africa (AUCIEFFA).

 

  1. Activities and Deliverables

 

The African Union Commission seeks the services of a qualified professional to execute the role of Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant.

 

    1. The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant is responsible for:

 

  1. Designing and managing databases to store programme data and ensure accurate reporting.
  2. Maintaining and regularly updating M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records.
  3. Regularly collecting, compiling, analyzing, and synthesizing data and monitoring project progresses against established indicators and targets.
  4. Assisting in the administration of surveys, assessments, evaluations, and other data collection activities, including questionnaire preparation, data entry, and initial analysis.
  5. Maintaining organized records of M&E documents, reports, datasets, tools, and supporting evidence for audit and reporting purposes.
  6. Conducting regular data quality checks and support data verification exercises to ensure completeness, accuracy, consistency, and reliability of reported information
  7. Following up with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders on submission of required monitoring data and reporting information, under the guidance of the M&E Officer.
  8. Providing regular updates on programme achievements, challenges, and risks to program team and stakeholders
  9. Assisting the preparations of monitoring reports, dashboards, data visualizations, and other knowledge products
  10. Supporting the preparation of periodic project progress reports, including data summaries, indicator tracking tables, and supporting documentation for governance structures such as the Technical Working Group (TWG), Project Management Team (PMT), and Project Steering Committee (PSC).
  1. Supporting the organization of M&E-related meetings, workshops, training sessions, and learning events, including preparation of materials and documentation of proceedings.
  2. Supporting the documentation and dissemination of evaluation findings, lessons learned, and good practices.
  3. Coordinating routine communication with implementing partners and AU Member States regarding submission of monitoring data and reporting requirements.
  4. Supporting the operationalization of the AU Gender and Youth Observatory (AUGYO) through data management, documentation and reporting support.
  5. Performing any other related duties assigned by the supervisor.

 

    1. Deliverables

 

With guidance and under supervision of the Regional Programme Coordinator and working closely with the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, the Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant will deliver, at a minimum, the following:

  • Routine programme monitoring data collected, compiled, verified, and recorded under approved M&E systems in a timely manner.
  • M&E databases, tracking tools, and reporting templates maintained and updated regularly with accurate and complete information.
  • Monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc monitoring and reporting inputs and reports prepared and submitted according to programme requirements.
  • Data quality assurance protocols developed.
  • Consolidated data summaries, dashboards, factsheets, and other knowledge products developed to support programme monitoring and decision-making.
  • Programme achievements, lessons learned, success stories, and good practices documented and compiled for reporting, learning, and knowledge management purposes.
  • Any other related assignment assigned by the Regional Project Coordinator in support of the EAGER Project

 

  1. Reporting and Supervision

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant will report to the Regional Programme Coordinator and work under the supervision of the Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD) of the African Union Commission.

 

  1. Qualifications and Work Experience Required

 

a) Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Social Sciences, International Development, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.

b) Minimum of three years of relevant experience supporting monitoring, evaluation, reporting, or data management functions within development, gender equality, education, or related programmes.

c) Demonstrated experience in data collection, data entry, data management, and preparation of monitoring reports.

d) Experience supporting the use of M&E tools, databases, tracking systems, and data visualization platforms.

e) Basic understanding of results-based management (RBM), monitoring frameworks, indicators, and reporting processes.

f) Knowledge and experience in collecting and managing gender-sensitive data and indicators is an advantage.

g) Strong analytical skills with the ability to organize, interpret, and present programme data in a clear and concise manner.

h) Good written and verbal communication skills, including experience in preparing reports, summaries, and documentation.

i) Experience working with development partners, government institutions, or international organizations, preferably within the African development context.

j) Proficiency in relevant data management and reporting tools (e.g., Excel, databases, data visualization tools, or other M&E information management systems).

 

  1. Language Requirement

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant should be proficient in English and at least one of the African Union working languages. Good command of French and/or Portuguese is an advantage. 

 

  1. Terms of Payment and Duration

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant shall be remunerated based on experience, task load and will be guided by AUC considerations on equivalent professional level and rates. The contract will cover a 12-month period, with the possibility to extend based on successful performance.

APPEL A CANDIDATURES

COORDONNATEUR(TRICE) NATIONAL(E) ADJOINT(E) DU PROJET RIZPLUS

Référence : CON-068/MG-RIZPLUS/2026

Date de lancement : 03 juillet 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer la mise en œuvre du Projet de Productivité et de Résilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux (RIZPLUS), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultant individuel objet du présent appel à candidatures.

2. Sous la supervision du Coordonnateur National, le consultant aura pour mission principale de : (i) assister et conseiller le Coordonnateur National dans la coordination stratégique du Projet et (ii) assurer la coordination opérationnelle et technique au quotidien. A ce titre, il/elle apportera un appui managérial à la gestion, la supervision et le suivi des activités ainsi que des résultats de l’équipe de l’UGP et des UGPR, afin d’engager plus rapidement les activités, accélérer le taux de décaissement et améliorer le suivi de la mise en œuvre ainsi que le reporting de l’équipe interne comme des prestataires. 

Le lieu d’affectation est à Antananarivo, Madagascar (siège de l'UGP RIZPLUS). La durée du contrat est fixée jusqu’au 29 décembre 2028, sous réserve d’une évaluation annuelle satisfaisante des performances du consultant. Le démarrage de la prestation est prévu au début du mois de septembre 2026.

3. Les Termes de Référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être envoyés aux candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s qui en font la demande à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous. Les coordonnées complètes du (de la) candidat(e) devront être clairement indiquées dans la demande.

4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZPLUS invite les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services cidessus. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection des Consultants Individuels prévues dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) pour les fournitures, travaux, services autres que les services de consultants » 6ème édition, Février 2025. Les candidats les mieux classés à l’issue de l’évaluation des dossiers seront invités à un entretien.

5. Le consultant recherché doit répondre aux qualifications minimales suivantes :

  • Titulaire d’un diplôme de Master II en agronomie, management, sciences politiques, économie ou autre domaine pertinent pour la mission ;
  • Disposer d’au moins quinze (15) années d'expériences professionnelles, dont dix (10) années dans le secteur du développement rural ;
  • Avoir au moins cinq (5) années d'expérience dans la coordination, la direction des opérations ou le suivi-évaluation d'un projet de développement rural d'envergure nationale ;
  • Avoir au moins deux (2) ans d'expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : agriculture climato-intelligente (ACI), aménagement local, sécurisation foncière, irrigation, diffusion de technologie améliorée, socio-organisation ;
  • Justifier d’au moins deux (02) expériences professionnelles acquises dans le cadre de projets financés par la Banque mondiale, ainsi que d’une connaissance des procédures de la Banque Mondiale et/ou d’autres bailleurs de fonds ;
  • Justifier d'au moins une (1) expérience professionnelle réalisée dans l'une ou les deux régions d'Alaotra-Mangoro et de Sofia ;
  • Faire preuve de solides capacités de leadership, de management, d’analyse et de synthèse ;
  • Maîtrise des langues malagasy et française ;

Seront considérés comme des atouts :

  • Expérience dans la mise en place d'outils digitalisés de collecte de données et de suivi des activités ;
  • Expérience dans la gestion d'AGEX, d'assistants techniques et de prestataires titulaires de gros contrats ;
  • Maîtrise de la langue anglaise à l’écrit et à l’oral. 

6. Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s sont invités à déposer leurs dossiers de candidature, par courrier électronique ou sous pli fermé, comprenant une lettre de motivation, un CV détaillé avec références professionnelles, les copies certifiées conformes des diplômes ainsi que les attestations de travail.

Les dossiers de candidatures doivent parvenir au plus tard le 22 juillet 2026 à minuit pour les candidatures transmises par courrier électronique et entre 08h30 à 16h30 pour les candidatures déposées physiquement ou envoyés par courrier à l’adresse suivante :

101 Antananarivo – Madagascar

La mention suivante devra obligatoirement figurer sur l’objet de l’email ou sur l’enveloppe : « COORDONNATEUR NATIONAL ADJOINT DU PROJET RIZPLUS ».

Le Projet décline la responsabilité de la nonconsidération des candidatures ne respectant pas cette disposition obligatoire.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY                           :           MALAWI

NAME OF PROJECT          :           DIGITAL MALAWI ACCELERATION PROJECT

GRANT NO.                         :           IDA-E338-MW

ASSIGNMENT TITLE       :           HIRING OF DATA CENTRE CLOUD

ARCHITECT

REFERENCE NO.               :           MW-PPPC-555858-CS-INDV

 

The Government of Malawi has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of digital development in Malawi “Digital Malawi Acceleration Project” and intends to apply part of the proceeds for hiring of Data Centre Cloud Architect.

 

The overall aim of the Digital Malawi Acceleration Project is to increase access to, and inclusive use of, the internet and improve the Government's capacity to deliver digitally enabled services.

 

The project has four components, namely, Affordable broadband and secure data hosting, Interoperable and secure data platforms, High impact digital services and productive digital usage and Project management. Under Component 2, the Project is expected to cover the Next Generation Digital ID and identity verification services, including electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). To strengthen the capacity for the Department of e-Government, the project wishes to recruit a Data Centre Cloud Architect as part of the project support personnel. This position will be tenable at the National Data Centre in Lilongwe.

 

The Data Centre Cloud Architect, with the support of the Data Centre Manager, will carry out assigned duties and tasks with complete compliance with the best practice. The Data Centre Cloud Architect shall be responsible for designing, planning, and implementing cloud solutions within our data centre environment.

The Public Private Partnership Commission (PPPC) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The consultant shall be an individual with relevant qualifications and experience. The shortlisting criteria shall be:

  1. A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. Master's degree is not required but an added advantage with a minimum of five (5) years of experience in cloud architecture, with at least 2 years in a data centre environment.
  2. Should Demonstrate having relevant certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Microsoft Certified. Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or Google Professional Cloud Architect will be an added advantage.
  3. Should Demonstrate having experience in hybrid cloud environments, cloud security practices and tools, including identity and access management, encryption, and firewalls
  4. Demonstrate having a strong understanding of Data Centre technologies, including servers, storage, networking, and virtualization
  5. Should be proficient in infrastructure-as-a service.
  6. Should be familiar with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

 

A successful candidate will work with the Department of E-Government for a period of two (2) years renewable annually with the possibility of extending the contract subject to satisfactory performance. The performance will be measured based on timely submission and quality of all deliverables, advancement of the respective activities, and the feedback from management and technical team members at the e-Government Department focused on technical competency, professionalism, responsiveness, and teamwork.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Name of Project: Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR)

Grant No: P176371

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant (IC) to perform the Consultancy services to Develop an Integrated and Digitalized Statistical Information System for STATAFRIC.

Reference No.TN-STATAFRIC-AUC-481115-CS-INDV.

 

  1. Background

The African Union (AU) is committed to strengthening African statistical systems across the continent to support evidence-based policy-making, regional integration, and sustainable development. African statistical systems encompass national statistical offices (NSOs), regional economic communities (RECs), and continental institutions. However, data management systems across these entities are frequently fragmented, heterogeneous, and insufficiently interoperable. These structural challenges constrain the efficient exchange, consolidation, and dissemination of reliable and timely statistics at the continental level

 

Key challenges include:

  • Lack of standardized data formats and metadata schemas across NSOs and RECs.
  • Weak or absent automated data exchange mechanisms between national and continental systems.
  • Limited data governance frameworks governing quality assurance and access management.
  • Inadequate tools for real-time data visualization and dissemination to end-users.
  • Insufficient technical capacity within STATAFRIC to manage and maintain digital platforms.

To address these gaps, STATAFRIC intends to develop an integrated and digitalized statistical information system connecting national statistical systems, regional data platforms, and continental-level repositories. The system will support improved data collection, integration, analysis, and dissemination while ensuring interoperability and compliance with international statistical standards.

 

STATAFRIC therefore seeks to recruit a qualified individual consultant to design, develop and implementation of this integrated digital statistical information system at STATAFRIC.

 

 

 

 

  1. Objectives of the assignment

The consultancy specifically aims to:

 

  1. Conduct a structured diagnostic assessment of existing data management systems and information flows at STATAFRIC and within key partner institutions.
  2. Design a scalable, modular, and interoperable architecture for the integrated statistical information system.
  3. Develop and deploy a functional digital platform incorporating data ingestion, integration, governance, visualization, and dissemination capabilities.
  4. Establish secure and standards-compliant mechanisms for data exchange between NSOs, RECs, and STATAFRIC, developed in alignment and coordination with the parallel consultancy for the Continental Statistical Database (CSD), to ensure technical and data compatibility between the two systems.
  5. Define and implement data governance policies, metadata management standards, and quality assurance procedures.
  6. Build institutional capacity through structured training, technical documentation, and knowledge transfer.

 

  1. Expected Deliverables

All deliverables must be submitted in English and/or French, as agreed with STATAFRIC. Deliverables are subject to review and approval by STATAFRIC management before payment of the corresponding instalment.

 

#

Deliverable

Description and Minimum Content

Number of Days

D1

Methodological report and inception Report.

Detailed methodology; work plan with milestones; stakeholder engagement strategy; risk register; tools and data sources to be used.

10 days

D2

Diagnostic Assessment Report.

Documented review of existing systems; data flow maps; gap analysis across infrastructure, interoperability, security, and governance; prioritized system requirements; stakeholder consultation summary.

20 days

D3

System Architecture Design Document.

Architecture diagrams (high-level and component-level); technology stack with justification; data model and entity-relationship diagrams; integration architecture; security architecture; hosting strategy.

30 days

D4

Prototype / Operational Platform.

Deployed and functional platform with all modules (see Section 3.3); UAT (User Acceptance Testing) report signed off by STATAFRIC; source code repository with documentation; deployment guide.

20 days

D5

Data Exchange Framework & Interoperability Guidelines.

Exchange protocols and standards documentation; API specifications and documentation; integration connectors for ≥3 priority systems; testing and validation results.

20 days

D6

Training Materials & User Documentation.

Training programme agenda; presentation materials and exercises; administrator manual; end-user manual; maintenance and sustainability plan.

10 days

D7

Final Implementation Report.

Summary of all activities and outputs; lessons learned; recommendations for Phase 2 enhancements; handover checklist.

10 days

 

  1. Required Qualifications and Experience

 

    1. Academic Qualifications
  2. An advanced university degree (Master's level minimum) in one of the following fields: Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, or a closely related discipline.

 

    1. Professional Experience

The following experience is required:

 

  1. A minimum of ten (10) years of professional experience in the design, development, and implementation of large-scale information systems or data platforms.
  2. Demonstrated experience in statistical information systems, open data platforms, or national/regional data management initiatives.
  3. Proven experience in data interoperability, including the design of data exchange protocols, APIs, and automated pipelines.
  4. Practical knowledge of metadata standards (SDMX, DDI, or equivalent) and data governance frameworks.
  5. Experience conducting needs assessments and gap analyses in ICT or data management contexts.
  6. Experience in capacity building, including the design and delivery of technical training for institutional users.

 

The following experience is an asset:

 

  1. Prior experience with African Union institutions, regional economic communities, or national statistical offices in Africa.
  2. Experience in cloud infrastructure management (AWS, Azure, GCP or equivalent).
  3. Familiarity with international statistical standards frameworks (IMF SDDS, UN SDG data architecture, etc.).
  4. Proficiency in both English and French.

 

    1. Technical Competencies

Candidates should demonstrate proficiency in at least the following areas:

 

  1. Database design and management (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or equivalent relational/NoSQL systems).
  2. API development and web services (REST, SOAP).
  3. ETL pipeline design and data transformation tools.

Terms of Reference

 

Individual Consultant (IC) to perform the Consultancy Services to develop an Integrated and Digitalized Statistical Information System for STATAFRIC.

 

  1. Background and Context

The African Union (AU) is committed to strengthening African statistical systems across the continent to support evidence-based policy-making, regional integration, and sustainable development. African statistical systems encompass national statistical offices (NSOs), regional economic communities (RECs), and continental institutions. However, data management systems across these entities are frequently fragmented, heterogeneous, and insufficiently interoperable. These structural challenges constrain the efficient exchange, consolidation, and dissemination of reliable and timely statistics at the continental level.

 

Key challenges include:

  • Lack of standardized data formats and metadata schemas across NSOs and RECs.
  • Weak or absent automated data exchange mechanisms between national and continental systems.
  • Limited data governance frameworks governing quality assurance and access management.
  • Inadequate tools for real-time data visualization and dissemination to end-users.
  • Insufficient technical capacity within STATAFRIC to manage and maintain digital platforms.

To address these gaps, STATAFRIC intends to develop an integrated and digitalized statistical information system connecting national statistical systems, regional data platforms, and continental-level repositories. The system will support improved data collection, integration, analysis, and dissemination while ensuring interoperability and compliance with international statistical standards.

 

STATAFRIC therefore seeks to recruit a qualified individual consultant to design, develop and implementation of this integrated digital statistical information system at STATAFRIC.

 

  1. Objectives of the Consultancy

 

  1. General Objectives:

To design and implement an integrated and digitalized statistical information system for STATAFRIC that enables efficient, secure, and standards-compliant exchange, integration, and dissemination of official statistical data compiled and published by STATAFRIC from NSOs and RECs, across national, regional, and continental statistical systems. This assignment excludes internal administrative, accounting, logistics, or other non-statistical operational data used for STATAFRIC's day-to-day management.

 

  1. Specific Objectives

The consultancy services specifically aim to:

 

  1. Conduct a structured diagnostic assessment of existing data management systems and information flows at STATAFRIC and within key partner institutions.
  2. Design a scalable, modular, and interoperable architecture for the integrated statistical information system.
  3. Develop and deploy a functional digital platform incorporating data ingestion, integration, governance, visualization, and dissemination capabilities.
  4. Establish secure and standards-compliant mechanisms for data exchange between NSOs, RECs, and STATAFRIC, developed in alignment and coordination with the parallel consultancy for the Continental Statistical Database (CSD), to ensure technical and data compatibility between the two systems.
  5. Define and implement data governance policies, metadata management standards, and quality assurance procedures.
  6. Build institutional capacity through structured training, technical documentation, and knowledge transfer.

 

  1. Scope of Work

The consultant will carry out the following tasks:

 

  1. Diagnostic Assessment.

The consultant will undertake a comprehensive assessment of the existing statistical information landscape, including:

 

  1. Review and document the current data management systems, databases, and digital tools in use at STATAFRIC and at a representative sample of NSOs and RECs.
  2. Map existing data flows including submission mechanisms, formats, frequencies, and governance arrangements (aligned with the work of Specialized Technical Groups (STGs)) between national, regional, and continental actors.
  3. Identify critical gaps in infrastructure, data interoperability, security protocols, and governance frameworks.
  4. Assess the technical readiness of STATAFRIC's ICT environment (servers, network infrastructure, software stack, connectivity).
  5. Map key stakeholders involved in the production, management, and dissemination of statistical data for a defined set of priority thematic areas and indicators (based on SHaSA 2) and as recommended by Specialized Technical Groups (STGs).
  6. Produce a prioritized list of system requirements, covering both software and hardware/infrastructure needs, informed by stakeholder consultations.

 

 

  1. System Architecture Design.

Based on the diagnostic findings, the consultant will:

 

  1. Design comprehensive and modular architecture for the integrated statistical information system, specifying all major system components, both software/application components and underlying hardware/infrastructure components, and their interactions.
  2. Define technical specifications for each system component, including:
    • Data ingestion mechanisms (automated feeds, manual submission portals, API connectors).
    • Data integration and transformation services (ETL pipelines, harmonization rules).
    • Metadata management tools aligned with SDMX or equivalent international standards.
    • Data storage infrastructure (database design, cloud or hybrid hosting strategy).
    • Analytical processing and data visualization modules, enabling STATAFRIC staff and authorized users to explore, analyze, and visualize statistical data.
    • System monitoring, logging, and observability layer, to supervise system health, performance, and availability.
    • User access and identity management layer.
  3. Ensure the architecture is compatible with international standards for statistical data exchange, including SDMX, DDI, and relevant AU/STATAFRIC frameworks, as well as full interoperability with the Continental Statistical Database (CSD) currently under development.
  4. Define a technology stack justification, specifying recommended open-source or proprietary tools with rationale.
  5. Include data flow diagrams, entity-relationship diagrams, and integration architecture diagrams.

 

  1. Development of the Digital Platform.

The consultant will develop and deploy a functional operational platform including the following modules:

 

Module

Required Functionalities

Data Submission & Validation

Web-based submission portal; automated format validation; error flagging and feedback to data providers; support for batch uploads and API-based ingestion.

Data Transformation & Integration

Configurable ETL pipelines; data harmonization and unit standardization; conflict detection and resolution workflows; audit trail for all transformations.

Metadata Management

Metadata registry aligned with SDMX; variable-level documentation; versioning; linkage between datasets and their metadata.

Access & Identity Management

Role-based access control (RBAC); multi-factor authentication; user activity logging; tiered data access (public, institutional, restricted).

Data Visualization & Dissemination

Interactive dashboards with filtering and drill-down; exportable charts and tables; public-facing data portal; API for third-party data consumers.

System Administration

User and permission management interface; monitoring and alerting dashboard; backup and recovery management tools.

 

The platform must be designed for scalability (capable of onboarding all 55 AU member states), high availability (target uptime ≥ 99.5%), and maintainability by STATAFRIC technical staff post-deployment.

 

  1. Interoperability and Data Exchange.

 

  1. Design and document secure data exchange protocols between NSOs, RECs, and STATAFRIC, specifying authentication mechanisms, encryption standards, and data transfer formats.
  2. Develop RESTful APIs or automated data pipelines for programmatic data transmission, including API documentation and sandbox testing environment.
  3. Ensure full compliance with international statistical data exchange standards (SDMX, JSON-stat, CSV-W or equivalent).
  4. Define and test integration connectors for at least three (3) priority NSO or RECs systems identified during the diagnostic phase, selecting a mix of high-performing and middle-performing NSOs to ensure connectors are validated against realistic field challenges and varying levels of statistical and technical capacity.

 

  1. Security and Data Governance.
  1. Develop a data security policy covering data classification, encryption at rest and in transit, vulnerability management, and incident response.
  2. Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and define user roles, permissions, and access tiers for all system modules.
  3. Design a data governance framework specifying data ownership, stewardship responsibilities, quality assurance procedures, and data lifecycle management.
  4. Ensure compliance with applicable data protection regulations and AU data sovereignty principles.
  5. Define and implement data quality indicators and automated quality checks within the platform.

 

 

  1. Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer.
  1. Develop a structured training programme for STATAFRIC technical staff covering system administration, data management, and basic troubleshooting.
  2. Conduct hands-on training sessions (minimum two sessions) targeted at STATAFRIC technical staff and relevant technical stakeholders from NSOs and RECs who have the requisite IT/data management background to effectively absorb this technical training.
  3. Produce comprehensive technical documentation, including system architecture documents, installation and configuration guides, administrator manual, and end-user manual.
  4. Develop a system maintenance and sustainability plan, including recommended staffing profile, estimated annual maintenance costs, and upgrade roadmap for Years 2–3.

All deliverables must be submitted in English and/or French, as agreed with STATAFRIC. Deliverables are subject to review and approval by STATAFRIC management before payment of the corresponding instalment.

  3. Proven experience in data interoperability, including the design of data exchange protocols, APIs, and automated pipelines.

A titre de régularisation, la date de parution etait fixée au 23 mars 2026.

TERMES DE REFERENCE POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN INGENIEUR EN GENIE POUR LE PADCI

 

  1. Contexte et justification

 

Dans le cadre des réformes visant l’amélioration des rendements des systèmes numériques nationaux, le Gouvernement ivoirien, a sollicité un financement auprès de l'Association internationale de développement (IDA) (la "Banque mondiale") pour le Projet d’Accélération du Numérique en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI) pour un montant indicatif de 150 000 000 Dollars.

 

Aligné sur le Plan National de Développement (PND) 2021-2025, l’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) PADCI est d’accroitre l’utilisation inclusive et résiliente de l’internet haut débit et des services dans les secteurs ciblés.

 

Les activités principales du projet sont structurées sous quatre (04) composantes que sont :

  • 1) composante1 relative au Renforcement des fondements de l’écosystème d’innovation numérique ;
  • 2) composante 2 relative à l’Expansion de la connectivité à large bande à haut débit résiliente au changement climatique et de l’inclusion numérique ;
  • 3) composante 3 relative à l’Amélioration de la prestation et de l’adoption des services numériques du Gouvernement ;
  • 4) Composante 4 relative à la Gestion du Projet.

 

 

Le cadre institutionnel et organisationnel du Projet prévoit les organes suivants :

  • (i) un Comité de pilotage du Projet ;
  • (ii) une Cellule Technique de suivi ;
  • (iii) une Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP) ayant en charge la gestion des ressources du projet et qui assurera la coordination globale des aspects administratifs et fiduciaires du projet à travers ses différentes composantes.

 

Le personnel de cette UGP sera recruté conformément aux procédures en vigueur à la Banque mondiale.

 

Les présents Termes de Référence (TDR) visent à recruter un(e) Ingénieur(e) Génie Civil pour le PADCI afin de conduire les travaux nécessaires à la réalisation des objectifs cités plus haut.

 

  1. Rôles et responsabilités

Placé (e) sous l’autorité du Coordonnateur du Projet, l’Ingénieur(e) Génie Civil est chargé(e) d’assurer l’encadrement de la conception technique, la supervision et le suivi, de la mise en œuvre des activités de construction, de réhabilitation et d’installation d’équipements dans le cadre du PADCI depuis la phase d’étude jusqu’à la fin des travaux.

 

  1. Principales tâches de l’Ingénieur(e) Génie Civil

L’Ingénieur(e) Génie Civil aura pour tâches de :

  • Planifier et coordonner la mise en œuvre du projet pour tout ce qui concerne les interventions en infrastructures, y compris les phases de budgétisation, de conception et de construction, tout en veillant à l’alignement avec les objectifs stratégiques du projet et du bénéficiaire final ;
  • Animer des réunions hebdomadaires avec l’appui du maître d'œuvre ;
  • Prendre part à toute activité en rapport avec la préparation et l’exécution des travaux de construction, de réhabilitations et d’installation d’équipements ;
  • Analyser les études (architecturales et techniques) et fournir éventuellement les propositions de révision des plans avant la validation finale ;
  • Elaborer les Termes de Référence pour les appels à proposition et appels d’offres relatifs aux infrastructures ;

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Name of Project: Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR)

Grant No: P176371

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant (IC) to perform the Consultancy services to develop Guidelines for Phone Observatory Surveys in Africa.

Reference No. TN-STATAFRIC-AUC-546834-CS-INDV.

 

  1. Background

Demand for timely, high-frequency, and cost-effective data has led African countries to explore innovative ways of data collection and statistical production. Traditional face-to-face surveys, while essential, are often resource-intensive, time-consuming, and difficult to implement during emergencies, conflicts, pandemics, natural disasters, and other situations that restrict field operations. Recent advancements in mobile phone penetration, telecommunications infrastructure, digital technologies, and data science have created opportunities for conducting Phone Observatory Surveys (POS) as a complementary data collection mechanism. Phone surveys have proven effective in generating rapid information on socio-economic conditions, employment, food security, health, education, migration, business performance, agricultural activities, prices, and citizen perceptions.

 

Despite the growing uptake of phone surveys across Africa, there remains a significant gap in continent-specific, harmonised guidelines that address the unique challenges of the continent. The absence of such guidelines results in fragmented approaches, inconsistent methodologies, and data that are difficult to compare. Therefore, there is need to develop continental guidelines that provide methodological, operational, institutional, and ethical standards for the design, implementation, analysis, and dissemination of Phone Observatory Surveys in Africa. The guidelines will support National Statistical Offices (NSOs), Central Banks, Ministries, Research Institutions, Regional Economic Communities, and Development Partners in producing reliable, timely, and internationally comparable data through phone-based data collection systems.

 

It is against this background that Africa Union seeks to recruit a qualified consultant to develop comprehensive and practical Guidelines for Phone Observatory Surveys in Africa.

 

  1. Objectives of the assignment

The objective of this assignment is to develop harmonised, standardised and Africa-specific guidelines for the design and implementation of Phone Observatory Surveys across the continent. The specific objectives are to:

  1. Review and assess the existing international, continental and regional guidelines, frameworks, standards, and best practices for phone-based surveys.
  2. Assess the landscape of phone observatory surveys currently being conducted across African countries, identifying gaps, challenges, and lessons learned.
  3. Develop comprehensive, step-by-step guidelines covering all phases of a phone observatory survey, from design and sampling through to data dissemination and archiving.
  4. Propose a harmonised set of core indicators and modules that can be adapted for use.
  5. Provide recommendations for institutionalising phone observatories within national statistical systems and for ensuring their sustainability.

 

  1. Duration and Timeline

The Individual Consultant (IC) is expected to produce a guideline document within 90 days from the date of signing the consultancy services contract.

 

  1. Reporting and supervision

The Individual Consultant (IC) will work remotely with STATAFRIC staff and will provide regular updates according to the agreed timeline. The contract is proposed under the following terms and conditions:

 

  • The duration of this contract is three months.
  • The consultant is expected to send an updated C.V and a methodological note about the understanding of the entire assignment.

The Individual Consultant (IC) should have at least a master’s degree in statistics, demography, economics, Social Sciences, or a related field with at least 15 years of professional experience.

Develop comprehensive guidelines covering the following:

 

  1. Conceptual and Institutional Framework: Definitions and purpose of a Phone Observatory Survey, Typology of phone-based survey modes (CATI, IVR, SMS, mobile web), Legal, ethical, and data protection considerations, Institutional anchoring within the National Statistical System, Governance structures and coordination mechanisms.
  2. Survey Design and Planning: Thematic scope and selection of indicators, questionnaire design principles for phone-based surveys, adaptation of questionnaires for multilingual and low-literacy populations, survey length and respondent fatigue considerations.
  3. Sampling Methodology: Overview of sampling frames available in Africa, strategies for addressing coverage bias and phone ownership gaps, sample size determination and precision requirements, Weighting, and representativeness considerations.
  4. Technology and Infrastructure: Selection and configuration of CATI software platforms, Requirements for call center infrastructure (in-house vs. outsourced), data security and storage protocols, use of mobile-based platforms and open-source tools.
  5. Data Collection, Processing, and Quality Assurance: Field management and call scheduling, response rate monitoring and non-response analysis, data cleaning, editing, and imputation procedures, quality assurance frameworks and indicators.
  6. Data Analysis, Dissemination, and Use: Weighting and calibration procedures, Estimation and variance calculation methods, Reporting formats and dissemination platforms, Integration of phone survey data with other data sources.

 

  1. Validation and Finalisation:
  1. Undertake stakeholders’ validation and incorporate feedback received
  2. Submit the Final Guidelines Document

 

  1. Deliverables
  1. Methodological Report: A detailed report outlining the methodology to be used to undertake this consultancy and a stakeholder engagement strategy. This should be after submission of an inception report indicating the work plan with deliverables and timelines.
  2. Review/assessment Report: Summarizing findings from the assessment of existing practices and standards, and stakeholders’ consultations.
  3. Draft of the Guidelines: Including detailed recommendations for phone observatory surveys.
  4. Stakeholder validation Report: Summarizing feedback and input from stakeholders
  5. Report on presentation to STATAFRIC and wider stakeholders.
  6. Final Guidelines: Comprehensive and ready for adoption by relevant stakeholders.

 

  1. Duration and Timeline

The Individual Consultant (IC) is expected to produce a guideline document within 90 days from the date of signing the consultancy contract. 

 

  1. Reporting and supervision.

The consultant will work remotely with STATAFRIC staff and will provide regular updates according to the agreed timeline. The contract is proposed under the following terms and conditions:

 

  • The duration of this contract is three months.
  • The Individual Consultant must send an updated C.V. and a methodological note on the understanding of the assignment.

PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT COMMUNAUTAIRE INTEGRE AU BURUNDI (PRODECI-TURIKUMWE)

DEMANDE DE MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

 (SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)
