GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

COUNTRY                             : Bangladesh                          

NAME OF PROJECT           : Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience,

Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT) Project

SECTOR                                : Social Protection                                                                 

Loan No./Credit No.               : 77230-BD

Project ID No.                         : P508519

 

The People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing in the amount of US$ 200 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience, Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT)” Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

The project will include the following components:

Component 1 will support establishment and roll-out of a DSR and will finance i) the establishment of a DSR Implementation Unit at Department of Social Services (DSS) and a Coordination Unit at Finance Division (FD), ii) strengthening program administration for DSS cash transfer and livelihoods programs, iii) enhancing MIS systems, capacity building, and outreach. iv) conducting regular assessments and surveys for effective program management.

Component 2 will support strengthening cash transfer programs for the poor  in (i) Benefit Adequacy :Incentivizing increase in benefit levels commensurate to the poverty line, and creating a standardized benefit adequacy framework for future program budgeting and revision of allowance amounts for the selected cash transfer programs at DSS (ii) Citizen centric frontline delivery: Augmenting capacity of the frontline cadre of social workers to serve vulnerable groups, use the DSR for case management of ultra-poor, and create a standard beneficiary feedback loop (iii) Cash plus interventions for elderly and persons with disabilities:

Component 3 will support expansion of livelihoods support for the poor to enhance the self-reliance of poor communities by improving economic inclusion initiatives leveraging the Dynamic Social Registry for better targeting and outreach.

Component 4 will support contingent emergency response.

Some of the key activities to be undertaken under the project include, but not limited to, the following:

Works- There is no high-value works package.

Goods- There is no high-value goods package.

Services-

  • Selection of consulting firm for development of a Management Information System (MIS) of Dynamic Social Registry System (DSR) of DSS, estimated cost of $2.500 million under Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method.
  • Selection of consulting firm for Implementation Support firm for Cash Plus Interventions, estimated cost of $ 1.916 million under Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method.
  • Selection of consulting firm for Livelihood program support of DSS, estimated cost of $ 3.583 million under Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method.
  • Selection of consulting firm for upgradation / Development of DSS livelihood Programs System (RSS, RMC, Burn Victim & UCD), estimated cost of $ 1.416 million under Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method.
  • Selection of consulting firm for Outreach, DSR registration & application support, estimated cost of $ 3.341 million under Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method.

Non-consulting Services- There is no high-value non-consulting services package.

Procurement of contracts for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, under Investment Project Financing (IPF) financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Regulations: “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers-” Sixth Edition, February 2025 (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Regulations.

Specific procurement notices for contracts to be procured under the project will be announced, as they become available, on the World Bank External website, and in the local newspapers having wider circulation.

Prequalification of suppliers and contractors, if required and other methods of selection will be specified in the SPNs for any specific contract following the regulations.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above-mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below:

procnotices.bid_description: Longmen Wetland Conservation and Restoration Project
procnotices.contact_address: China
procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation for Bids (IFB)

Date: July 20, 2026

Bid No.: 0773-2610GNOEGCGK1869

IFB No.: 0773-2610GNOEGCGK1869

 

1. The Chinese Government has received a loan from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Ecosystem Restoration and Biodiversity Conservation Project and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan from the World Bank to payments under the Contract for Longmen Wetland Conservation and Restoration Project in Hejin City (Contract No.: SXHJ-C02).

 

2.The China Capital Tendering Co., Ltd. (the "Procurement Agent") entrusted by Hejin City Forestry Bureau (the "Employer"), now invites sealed bids from all eligible and qualified bidders for Longmen Wetland Conservation and Restoration Project in Hejin City, the main scope of which includes ecological revetment construction, key bird foraging ground construction, road renovation, wooden boardwalks, water system stepping stones, birdwatching pavilions, wetland management and monitoring stations, field observation stations for wetland birds, interpretive signages and guide boards, water quality monitoring points, environmental factor monitoring points, interpretive education corridors, greening and other related works. The construction period for all aforementioned works shall be 9 months, the maintenance period for the greening works within the above scope shall be 24 months (commencing on the date of satisfactory completion acceptance).

3. This bidding will be conducted in accordance with the National Competitive Bidding procedures. It is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers of the World Bank.

 

4. Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and inspect the Bidding Documents at the address given below from 16:00 on July 20, 2026 to 17:00 on August 31, 2026.

 

5. The attention of prospective Bidders is drawn to the eligibility and conflict of interest provisions under ITB Clause 4 of the Bidding Documents. All bidders found to have a conflict of interest shall be disqualified.

(a) Submission of audited financial statements or, if not required by the law of the bidder’s country, other financial statements for the last THREE [3] years (2023-2025) to demonstrate the current soundness of the bidder’s financial position and its prospective long-term profitability. procnotices.notice_text:
THE REPUBLIC OF SOUTH SUDAN

MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND IRRIGATION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

Country                  

South Sudan

 

Advert Start Date

20th  July, 2026

 

Advert Closing Date

10th August, 2026

 

Name of project

Regional Climate Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa

Project ID

P180171

 

IDA Grant no.  

E1920-SS

 

Assignment title

Contract Management Specialist (International Hire)

Reference no.

SS-MWRI-559230-CS-INDV

 

 

 

1. The Government of the Republic of South Sudan (GRSS) represented by the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation (MWRI) has received funding from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank, toward the Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP) for Eastern and Southern Africa (P1801711) and has applied for funding for the National WASH (NWASH) Project. Both Projects will be implemented under a single, joint Project Implementation Unit (PIU).  To strengthen the project implementation team, the MWRI intends to hire a Contract Management Specialist to join the PIU and provide the necessary technical and operational support to facilitate the implementation of the projects

 

2. The primary objective of the Contract Management Specialist assignment is to provide professional contract management by ensuring effective, timely and fiduciary compliant management of contract across all infrastructure components for the effective implementation of RCRP and NWP. The Specialist will ensure that all contractual processes related to the rehabilitation, construction, expansion, and maintenance of water supply and sanitation infrastructure under the RCRP and NWP Projects, as well as water resources management activities, are conducted in accordance with World Bank Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025 and international best practices. The Contract Management Specialist will play a critical role in strengthening the PIU’s capacity to plan, coordinate, manage complex contracts, mitigate implementation risks, and ensure timely and cost-effective delivery of project components, thereby contributing to the achievement of the project’s development objectives

 

3.  More details are provided in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The detailed Terms of Reference can be downloaded from the website The NGO Forum at https://comms.southsudanngoforum.org/c/tenders/8 . The ToR may also be obtained from the email address below: crfm.procurement@gmail.com  copied to crfmsouthsudan@gmail.com

 

4. The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation (MWRI) now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest to provide this Service. Interested individuals should provide information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), Copies of documentary evidence of academic qualifications, Membership of internationally recognized professional body / bodies, etc).  The shortlisting criteria will consider the requirements mentioned in the ToR:

Qualifications

The consultant must have the following minimum qualifications

  1. Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field from a recognized institution. Advanced professional certifications in contract management or project management (e.g., PMP, FIDIC Certified Contract Manager) are highly desirable.
  2. Must be a member of an internationally recognized professional body and in good standing.

 

Professional Experience

The consultant should have demonstrable experience in Contract Management and Administration-related activities as follows:

  1. General experience of 15 years in managing civil works contracts
  2. Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in contract management for at least three (3) large-scale infrastructure projects, preferably in the water sector.
  3. Experience in the administration and management of FIDIC Contracts, including Conditions of Contract for Construction, Plant and Design-Build, and EPC/Turnkey projects
  4. Proven track record in managing large value works and Plant Design, Supply, and Installation contracts, with direct responsibility for contract negotiation, implementation, and dispute resolution.
  5. Experience working on projects financed by international development institutions (e.g., World Bank, other MDBs) is required.
  6. International experience in at least two countries/regions, with demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge and build capacity of local counterparts.

Skills and Competencies

  1. In-depth knowledge of international contract standards, including FIDIC and other relevant procurement and contract management frameworks.
  2. Strong analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to address complex technical and contractual issues.
  3. Proficiency in contract management software and standard office applications (e.g., MS Office Suite, MS Project, AutoCAD).
  4. Excellent report-writing and communication skills in English;
  5. Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and under tight deadlines.
  6. High ethical standards, attention to detail, and demonstrated commitment to transparency and accountability in contract administration.

 

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Any false declaration will result in disqualification.

 

6. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Government officials or civil servants of the Republic of South Sudan will not be considered unless: (i) they are on leave of absence without pay or have resigned or retired six months prior to the date of the advert; and (ii) their employment will not create Conflict of Interest. An invitation to an oral interview will follow for shortlisted candidates.

 

7. Further information can be obtained at the address below during the following office hours 09:00 and 16:00 hours local time from Monday to Friday excluding public holidays.

 

8.Expression of interest shall be delivered by 10th August 2026 at 1600 hours local time, by email to:  crfm.procurement@gmail.com and copies to crfmsouthsudan@gmail.com . Quote the Assignment title and Reference Number in the subject row.

procnotices.notice_text:
The Clean Energy and Power Trade Development in Southeast Asia Project of the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach Accelerating Sustainable Energy Transition/MPA ASET

Project/Grant No.: P181555 / IDA -E3430

Assignment: Individual Consultants (Experts) for the MPA ASET Project

The ASEAN Centre for Energy has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Clean Energy and Power Trade Development in Southeast Asia Project of the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach Accelerating Sustainable Energy Transition/MPA ASET (P181555) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to finance consulting services for a number of Individual Consultants.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for each expert position, including the scope of the services, required qualifications and experience, level of effort and the expected commencement date can be downloaded from the following link:

https://aseanenergy.org/opportunities/procurement/expression-of-interest-recruitment-of-individual-consultants-for-multiple-assignments

The Consultant shall demonstrate that they possess the qualification and relevant experience required for the position as specified in respective terms of reference. The qualifications of the Consultant will be evaluated against, among others, the following criteria:

  1. Specific experience relevant to the assignment as indicated in the individual TOR
  2. Qualifications and competencies for the Assignment             
  3. Ability to work with and transfer knowledge and skills to counterpart staff

The ASEAN Centre for Energy now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.).

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 6th Edition dated February 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Expressions of interest, clearly quoting the Assignment Title and Procurement Reference Number of each relevant position in the Subject line of the email, must be delivered in writing by e-mail no later than 31 July 2026. Interested Consultants shall use the following CV template provided in this EOI.

ASEAN CENTRE FOR ENERGY 

Attn: Project Management Unit

E-mail: asetprocurement@aseanenergy.org

Anuncio Específico de Adquisiciones

 

Solicitud de Ofertas

Obras

(Proceso de dos Sobres, Sin precalificación)

Contratante:              MINISTERIO DE OBRAS PÚBLICAS Y DE TRANSPORTE

Proyecto:                    PROYECTO DE TRANSPORTE E INFRAESTRUCTURA RESILIENTE DE EL SALVADOR

Título del contrato:   “CONSTRUCCIÓN DEL BYPASS DE APOPA, ENTRE CARRETERAS SAL38E-CA04N, DISTRITOS DE CIUDAD DELGADO, TONACATEPEQUE Y APOPA, DEPARTAMENTO DE SAN SALVADOR: TRAMO I Y TRAMO II”

País:                           EL SALVADOR

N.° de préstamo/N.: BIRF No. 9602-SV y BIRF No. 9836-SV

SDO N. °:                   01/2026 (SV-MOPT-533875-CW-RFB)

Emitido el:                 28 DE MARZO DE 2026

  1. El Gobierno de la República de El Salvador ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para la totalidad del costo del Proyecto de Transporte e Infraestructura Resiliente de El Salvador, y se propone utilizar parte  de dichos fondos para efectuar los pagos estipulados en los Contratos del proceso: “Construcción del Bypass de Apopa, entre Carreteras SAL38E – CA04N, distritos de Ciudad Delgado, Tonacatepeque y Apopa, Departamento de San Salvador: Tramo I y Tramo II”
  2. El Ministerio de Obras Públicas y de Transporte, MOPT, invita a los Licitantes elegibles a presentar Ofertas en sobres cerrados para la Construcción del Tramo I y del Tramo II del Bypass de Apopa, una carretera con una longitud total de 13.07 km incluyendo sus intercambiadores. La sección geométrica de la carretera consiste en cuatro carriles, dos por sentido, separados por una barrera tipo New Jersey, incluyendo hombros interiores y exteriores que comparten una ciclo-ruta a lo largo del proyecto, con un ancho total de la carretera de 22.40 m más la distancia de los taludes de corte y relleno, siendo el tipo de superficie de la carretera de concreto asfáltico.
  3. El proyecto se desarrollará en dos tramos (dos lotes), cuya ubicación, particularidades y plazo de construcción se detallan a continuación:

LOTE

NOMBRE

DESCRIPCION

PLAZO DE EJECUCIÓN

1

TRAMO I:

ESTACIÓN 0+000 A 1+616

El Tramo I, posee una longitud aproximada de 4.12 km e incluye la construcción de siete estructuras: un Puente Atirantado de 400 m de longitud, de los cuales 320 m son atirantados y 80 m son puente convencional; el Puente Eje C (incorporación), con una longitud de 323 m compuesto por un viaducto de 9 tableros de vigas isostáticos de 35 a 37 m; el Puente Eje D (salida), de 325 m, también conformado por un viaducto de 9 tableros similares; - el Paso Inferior 0+540, el Puente 0+820, el Puente 1+010 y el Paso Inferior 1+400 - con longitudes que oscilan entre 35.00 y 43.70 m, todas con configuración de tramo isostático.

 

 1,080 días

contados a partir de que se emita la orden de inicio

2

TRAMO II: ESTACIÓN 1+616 A 4+825

El Tramo II tiene una longitud aproximada de 8.95 km, incluyendo sus intercambiadores, e incluye la construcción de un puente tipo cajón postensado a tres claros, pasos inferiores, puentes con longitudes variables y una caja vehicular; diseñadas mayoritariamente con sistemas de vigas AASHTO en configuración isostática, seleccionadas por su eficiencia estructural y adaptabilidad a las condiciones del terreno. Las longitudes de los puentes varían entre 35.00 m y 290.00 m, y responden a las necesidades particulares de cada punto del trazo del proyecto.

 

 

720 días

contados a partir de que se emita la orden de inicio

    

Los Licitantes pueden presentar Ofertas por un lote o por ambos, tal como se define en la Solicitud de Ofertas (SDO).

4. La licitación se llevará a cabo mediante adquisiciones competitivas internacionales utilizando el método de Solicitud de Ofertas (SDO), conforme a lo previsto en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial Sexta Edición Septiembre de 2025 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”) y se encuentra abierta a todos los Licitantes elegibles, como se los define en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.

 

5. Las Ofertas se evaluarán de conformidad con el procedimiento establecido en los documentos de licitación. Se aplicarán las siguientes ponderaciones: para los Criterios con Puntaje (incluidos los factores técnicos y los factores que no están asociados al precio): 50%, y para el costo de la Oferta: 50%.

 

6. Los Licitantes elegibles interesados podrán adquirir el documento de licitación en idioma Español a partir de las 00:00 horas del 30 de marzo de 2026, descargando gratuitamente del sistema de compras públicas COMPRASAL (www.comprasal.gob.sv) previo registro en el sistema. Asimismo los documentos estarán disponibles en la página web www.mop.gob.sv  o descargarlo en el link:

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1l0AzkcEAsMqw6S1-tYY9nRZcLZEmf5gU?usp=sharing

En el caso de descargar por medio del link o la página web del Ministerio de Obras Públicas, favor enviar un correo a ucp.bypassapopa@mop.gob.sv proporcionando: nombre de la empresa, correo electrónico para notificaciones, números de teléfono y país de origen.

Asimismo, podrán adquirirlo directamente en la Unidad de Compras Públicas (UCP) del MOPT ubicada en el Módulo “E”, Plantel La Lechuza Km 5 ½, Carretera a Santa Tecla, frente al Estado Mayor de la Fuerza Armada, San Salvador, a partir del 7 de abril de 2026, en cuyo caso el interesado deberá contar con un dispositivo de almacenamiento (USB)

7. Las Ofertas deberán dirigirse a la dirección que se indica al final de este llamado a más tardar a las 10:00 a.m. (Hora de El Salvador) del día 21 de mayo de 2026. No está permitida la presentación electrónica de las Ofertas. Las ofertas recibidas fuera del plazo establecido serán rechazadas. Los sobres exteriores de la Oferta marcados como “OFERTA ORIGINAL” y los sobres interiores marcados como “PARTE TÉCNICA” se abrirán públicamente en presencia de los representantes designados por los Licitantes y cualquier persona que decida asistir, en la dirección indicada al final de este llamado, a partir de las 10:15 a.m. (Hora de El Salvador) del día 21 de mayo de 2026.   Todos los sobres marcados como “PARTE FINANCIERA” permanecerán sin abrir y se mantendrán bajo custodia segura del Contratante hasta la segunda apertura pública de las Ofertas.

8. Todas las Ofertas deben ir acompañadas de: (i) una “Declaración de Mantenimiento de la Oferta”; y (ii) Declaración del Método de Contratación de Mano de Obra Local.

9. Se llama la atención sobre las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones que requieren que el Prestatario divulgue información sobre la propiedad efectiva del adjudicatario, como parte de la Notificación de Adjudicación de Contrato, utilizando el Formulario de Divulgación de la Propiedad Efectiva incluido en el documento de licitación.

procnotices.notice_text:
SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA

BRASIL – Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima - MMA

Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia - ASL BRASIL 2

Acordo de Doação N.º TF0B6898-BR – Banco Mundial

Número de Referência: BR-FGV-558236-CS-INDV

 

 

Escopo: Seleção e contratação de consultoria individual especializada em sistematização de diretrizes técnicas para seleção de espécies e definição de arranjos de restauração da vegetação nativa no Estado do Pará, no âmbito do Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil – Fase 2).

 

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 009/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETULIO VARGAS, ou simplesmente FGV, torna público que está aberto o prazo para consultores individuais elegíveis interessados na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à consultoria individual especializada em sistematização de diretrizes técnicas para seleção de espécies e definição de arranjos de restauração da vegetação nativa no Estado do Pará. Os consultores individuais interessados deverão demonstrar que são qualificados e que têm a experiência para desempenhar o serviço, conforme descrito no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes

 

           As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas até dia 31 de julho de 2026, às 23:59 horas, para o e-mail  asl2.compras@fgv.br. As Manifestações deverão estar identificadas como SMI Nº 009/2026 – Diretrizes Técnicas PA. O(a) consultor(a) individual deverá demonstrar capacidade para atuar na sistematização de diretrizes técnicas para seleção de espécies e definição de arranjos de restauração da vegetação nativa no Estado do Pará, garantindo que as atividades ocorram conforme o planejamento, que engloba o levantamento, a análise e a sistematização de bases de dados e diretrizes técnicas e metodológicas para subsidiar o desenvolvimento de uma plataforma digital de apoio à tomada de decisão. O(a) consultor(a) individual interessado(a) deverá apresentar o seu currículo e demais documentos que comprovem a sua expertise, de acordo com os requisitos definidos no Termo de Referência.

 

Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse não pressupõe qualquer compromisso de contratação. Os(as) consultores(as) individuais elegíveis serão avaliados(as) de acordo com as normas do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição de setembro de 2023”.

 

Informações adicionais sobre o processo seletivo poderão ser solicitadas pelo endereço eletrônico asl2.compras@fgv.br

 

A Fundação Getúlio Vargas entrará em contato somente com os(as) consultores(as) individuais elegíveis para a próxima etapa do processo.

Le Gouvernement Malagasy a reçu crédit de la Banque Internationale pour financer le PROJET DE TRANSFORMATION DE L’ACCES ET DE L’APPRENTISSAGE A MADAGASCAR (TALIM), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché pour la location de salle et divers services, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, sauf pour les paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de lettre de crédit.

    3. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à une demande de cotation telle que définie dans le « Règlement applicable aux Emprunteurs – Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement de la Banque Mondiale version Juillet 2016 mis à jour en Février 2025 (« le Règlement de passation des marchés »), et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans les Règles de passation des marchés.

 

     4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Facilitation de Projet (UFP) ; et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres durant les heures de bureau, du lundi au vendredi de 09h00 à 17h00 à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

     6. Les offres devront être soumises sous pli fermé avec la mention 003-26/AAO/UFP/TALIM-Ni – LOCATION DE SALLE ET DIVERS SERVICES REPARTIS EN HUIT (08) LOTS : LOT N°, à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 20 août 2026 à dix heures (10h00). La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires présents à l’adresse ci-dessous et à la date et heure limite prévue.  

     7. La garantie d’offres n’est pas requise.

procnotices.contact_address: DRC
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Entrepreneurship and Small Medium Enterprises
procnotices.notice_text:
Avis Spécifique d’Appel d’Offres (AAO)

(Processus à Une Enveloppe)

 

AON N° ZR-TRANSFORME-559969-GO-RFB  

 

République Démocratique du Congo

Ministère de l’Entrepreneuriat et Développement des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises

 

UNITE DE COORDINATION DU PROJET TRANSFORME/RDC

 

PROJET D’AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ENTREPRENEURES ET MISE À NIVEAU DES PME POUR LA TRANFORMATION ECONOMIQUE ET L’EMPLOI
« TRANSFORME / RDC »

(Source de financement : Crédit n°7101-ZR & Don E0280-ZR)

 

 

Projet : Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME)

Référence : Crédit n°7101-ZR & Don E0280-ZR

Intitulé du Marché : Acquisition d’une chaîne complète de production textile et d’étiquetage pour le Centre de PME JOSPRINT à Mbuji-Mayi

Référence de l’AON : ZR-TRANSFORME-559969-GO-RFB

 

Emis le : Lundi, le 20 juillet 2026

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un prêt et un don de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement pour financer le coût du Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME-RDC) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce prêt pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché : Acquisition d’une chaîne complète de production textile et d’étiquetage pour le Centre de PME JOSPRINT à Mbuji-Mayi.

 

  1. L’Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME-RDC) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour la réalisation de marché d’Acquisition d’une chaîne complète de production textile et d’étiquetage pour le Centre de PME JOSPRINT à Mbuji-Mayi dans la Province du Kasaï-Oriental) pour un délai minimum de livraison de 4 mois.

 

  1. La passation du Marché sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale, Appel d’offres national (AON) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) » septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

 

  1. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès de l’Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Autonomisation des Femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la Transformation économique et l’Emploi (UCP/TRANSFORME-RDC), à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : de 9 heures à 16 heures (heure locale, TU+1) ou sur le site web « www.transforme.cd.

 

  1. Le Document d’Appel d’Offres en langue française, peut être acheté par tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de 150 USD (Cent cinquante dollars américains). La méthode de paiement sera le dépôt direct du montant au compte du Projet TRANSFORME/RDC logé à la RAWBANK, Intitulé du compte : Ministère des Finances v/c TRANSFORME-DAO, numéro du comte : 05100 – 05101 – 00003991006 – 61 (USD) « Code Swift : RAWBCDKIXXX ». Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par voie électronique ou téléchargé à partir d’un site web autorisé du Projet TRANSFORME « www.transforme.cd ». Seules les offres des soumissionnaires ayant acheté le Dossier d’Appel d’offres seront acceptées.

 

  1. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse suivante au plus tard le 21 août 2026 à 14h00’. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et de toute personne choisissant d’être présente à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, le 21 août 2026 à 14h30’.

 

  1. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une garantie de l’offre (Garantie bancaire), pour un montant de treize mille cinq cent trente dollars américains (USD 13 530).
  2. L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

1. O Estado da Bahia, através da Secretaria de Infraestrutura (SEINFRA) recebeu

e Resiliência das Rodovias do Estado da Bahia (PRÓ-RODOVIAS) e pretende destinar
parte dos recursos a pagamentos no âmbito do acordo de empréstimo para a Contratação
de Projetos e Obras para supressão de pontos críticos em Estradas Vicinais - Consórcio
Chapada Forte.

2. Convidam-se os Licitantes elegíveis a apresentar Ofertas lacradas para
Contratação de empresa especializada, para a elaboração de Projetos de Engenharia e
Execução de Obras de Construção de bueiros tubulares e celulares, passagens molhadas,
melhoria de greide e pontes pré-moldadas com vãos de 10, 20 e 30 metros, incluindo
serviços de terraplenagem, drenagem, sinalização, analise socioambiental e demais
serviços associados para a supressão de pontos críticos e melhoria da infraestrutura viária
em trechos da malha rodoviária municipal, rurais e não pavimentadas, do Estado da Bahia,
no Consórcio Intermunicipal de Desenvolvimento do Circuito do Diamante da Chapada
Diamantina (CIDCD) - Chapada Forte.
Os Licitantes elegíveis poderão obter mais informações junto a Comissão Permanente de

Specific Procurement Notice

 

Request for Bids

Goods

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

 

Country: Republic of Cabo Verde

Name of Project: Digital Cabo Verde

Contract Title: Purchase of equipment and other supplies/materials for the Digital Service Team

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA 7797 | P171099

RFB Reference No.: 104/DCVP/UGPE/2025_2

Data: May 15, 2026

Extension date: July 20, 2026

 

1. The Government of the Republic of Cabo Verde has received financing from the International Development Association (hereafter named “World Bank”) toward the cost of the Digital Cabo Verde Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Purchase of IT Equipment

2. The implementing agency, Unidade de Gestão de Projectos Especiais (UGPE) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Purchase of equipment for the Registry, Notary, and Identification Services, Transportation, Citizen Center, and employees of the Digital Services Team and the Embassy of Cape Verde in Portugal.

3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016 and revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from Unidade de Gestão de Projectos Especiais and inspect the bidding document during office hours from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. (local time), during working days, at the address given below.

5. The bidding document in English language only, can be found published at the following website UGPE: https://ugpe.gov.cv/concursos and MF: https://www.mf.gov.cv/web/mf/outras-publicacoes.

8. Electronic submission will be permitted. Please check the bidding document for instructions.

9. Late Bids will be rejected.

11. All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security in form of a Bank Guarantee. Please check the bidding document for more instructions on Bid Security.

12. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

13. In addition, please refer to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.bid_description: Consulting Services for Revision and Harmonization of the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for the Conduct of Investigations – Office of Internal Oversight (OIO), African Union Commission
procnotices.contact_address: Africa Union HeadquartersP.O.BOX 3243Tel: 251-11-5-517700webmaster: webmaster@africa-union.orgAddis
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 

Country: Ethiopia

Name of Project: The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project

Grant No: P180117

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Revision and Harmonization of the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for the Conduct of Investigations – Office of Internal Oversight (OIO), African Union Commission

 

Reference No. ET-AUC-524051-CS-QCBS

 

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include developing an updated, harmonized, and enforceable Investigation SOP, aligned with AU legal, HR, ethics, data-protection, and disciplinary frameworks, and consistent with international best practices (e.g., UN Investigation Guidelines, CII Standards).

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

 

The African Union Commission now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • At least 10 years of proven experience in governance, oversight, investigations, integrity systems, public sector accountability, institutional reform, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in the development, revision, harmonization, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), investigation manuals, policies, and regulatory frameworks for international organizations, public institutions, supreme audit institutions, or oversight bodies.
  • Proven track record of conducting assignments for international organizations, multilateral institutions, regional organizations, governments, or oversight entities, preferably within Africa.
  • Demonstrated expertise in administrative investigations, misconduct investigations, fraud and corruption investigations, whistleblower protection, ethics and compliance frameworks.
  • Experience in organizational diagnostics, process mapping, business process re-engineering, and change management initiatives.
  • Proven capacity to facilitate stakeholder consultations, workshops, and validation exercises involving senior management and technical experts.
  • Availability of a multidisciplinary team covering investigations, legal and HR policy, change management, and information governance.
  • Excellent knowledge of international standards and best practices relating to investigations, including relevant guidance from the United Nations system, multilateral development banks, and professional investigative bodies.

CONSULTING SERVICES FOR REVISION AND HARMONIZATION OF THE STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) FOR THE CONDUCT OF INVESTIGATIONS – OFFICE OF INTERNAL OVERSIGHT (OIO), AFRICAN UNION COMMISSION

 

REF: ET-AUC-524051-CS-QCBS

 

  1. Background

This assignment supports the African Union Commission’s governance, ethics, and integrity agenda by strengthening the Office of Internal Oversight (OIO)’s investigative framework in line with Agenda 2063. It forms part of capacity-building initiatives supported by partners, including the World Bank (Biashara Project), and collaboration with oversight institutions across the AU Organs and Agencies.

 

Revising and harmonizing the Investigation Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) will reduce procedural risks, strengthen due-process safeguards, improve consistency and timeliness in investigations, and enhance the implementation of oversight recommendations. The assignment will also reinforce accountability, transparency, and institutional performance across the African Union system.

 

  1. Objective of the Assignment

To develop an updated, harmonized, and enforceable Investigation SOP, aligned with AU legal, HR, ethics, data-protection, and disciplinary frameworks, and consistent with international best practices (e.g., UN Investigation Guidelines, CII Standards).

 

The SOP package shall include:

 

  • Revised SOP text ;
  • User-friendly toolkits (templates, checklists, process maps);
  • An Investigator’s Charter ;
  • Guidance integrating human-rights-based and peace-operations-related investigative requirements;
  • An implementation and change-management plan.

 

  1. Scope of Work

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

 

  1. Document Review & Benchmarking

Review current AU/OIO policies, SOPs, manuals, and compare them with international standards and comparator organizations.

 

  1. Process Diagnostics & Gap Analysis

Identify gaps and bottlenecks across the full investigation cycle: intake, assessment, prioritization, evidence handling, digital evidence, interviews, confidentiality, reporting, referrals, cooperation with HRMD/OLC.

 

  1. Stakeholder Consultations

Structured consultations with OIO (Investigations, Audit Divisions), OLC, HRMD, MIS, Finance, and selected AU Organs/Agencies.

 

  1. Draft Revised SOP & Toolkits

Prepare the SOP, flowcharts, decision trees, templates (intake, interview plans, evidence logs, chain-of-custody, report templates).

 

  1. Compliance Alignment

Integrate due-process guarantees, data protection, whistleblower protection, retaliation prevention, records management, and e-discovery requirements.

  1. Implementation & Change-Management Plan

Develop a roadmap for dissemination, training, communication, indicators (KPIs), and risk mitigation measures.

 

  1. Finalization & Validation

Facilitate validation (virtual or in-person), consolidate comments, and produce the final SOP package.

 

  1. Schedule for Completion of Tasks
  • Week 1: Inception Report (methodology, detailed workplan, stakeholder mapping)
  • Week 3 : Diagnostic & Gap Analysis Report
  • Week 6 : Draft SOP + toolkits
  • Week 8: Validation workshop and revised draft
  • Week 10: Final SOP package + implementation plan

 

  1. Duration of the Assignment
  • Estimated duration: 10 weeks
  • Expected commencement date: Upon contract signature.
  • The assignment shall be completed within ten (10) weeks from the date of commencement.

 

  1. Deliverables for the Assignment

  1. Consultant’s Qualifications and Team Composition

Firm Qualification

 

The consulting firm shall demonstrate:

 

  • At least 10 years of proven experience in governance, oversight, investigations, integrity systems, public sector accountability, institutional reform, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in the development, revision, harmonization, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), investigation manuals, policies, and regulatory frameworks for international organizations, public institutions, supreme audit institutions, or oversight bodies.
  • Proven track record of conducting assignments for international organizations, multilateral institutions, regional organizations, governments, or oversight entities, preferably within Africa.
  • Demonstrated expertise in administrative investigations, misconduct investigations, fraud and corruption investigations, whistleblower protection, ethics and compliance frameworks.
  • Experience in organizational diagnostics, process mapping, business process re-engineering, and change management initiatives.
  • Proven capacity to facilitate stakeholder consultations, workshops, and validation exercises involving senior management and technical experts.
  • Availability of a multidisciplinary team covering investigations, legal and HR policy, change management, and information governance.
  • Excellent knowledge of international standards and best practices relating to investigations, including relevant guidance from the United Nations system, multilateral development banks, and professional investigative bodies.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing training materials, toolkits, guidance notes, and implementation frameworks to support institutional adoption of new procedures.
  • Experience working in multilingual environments, with the capacity to deliver all outputs in both English and French.
  • Evidence of successful completion of at least three similar assignments within the last five years.

 

Team Lead – Investigations Policy

 

  • Advanced degree in Law, Public Administration, Criminology, Investigations, or related field
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in administrative or forensic investigations within AU/UN/EU or similar institutions
  • Demonstrated experience drafting SOPs, policies, or governance frameworks
  • Strong knowledge of due process, data-protection, whistleblower protection, and disciplinary frameworks
  • Experience designing and delivering training for investigators
  • Bilingual (English/French)

 

Legal / HR Policy Expert

 

  • Advanced degree in Law, HR, Public Administration, or equivalent
  • Minimum 7 years of experience with disciplinary frameworks and HR/legal policies in AU/UN/EU or similar institutions
  • Expertise in due-process safeguards, misconduct procedures, administrative law
  • Experience with policy harmonization and regulatory reforms
  • Bilingual proficiency desirable

 

Change-Management & Training Specialist

 

  • Advanced degree in organizational development, HR, public administration, or similar
  • Minimum 7 years of experience in change management, institutional capacity building, and training programme design
  • Experience developing training toolkits, communication plans, and rollout strategies
  • Experience supporting adoption of new procedures in international organisations

 

IT / Governance (Records & e-Discovery) Expert

 

  • Degree in Information Systems, Digital Governance, Cybersecurity, or related field
  • 5–7 years of experience in e-discovery, digital evidence management, records governance
  • Experience with chain-of-custody, data protection, and case-management systems
  • Knowledge of oversight, audit, or legal digital workflows

Estimated Level of Effort

 

  • Team Lead: 30–40 days

  • IT/Governance Expert: 8–12 days

 

  1. Data, Services, and Facilities to be Provided by the Client

The African Union Commission will provide:

 

  • Access to relevant AU legal instruments, Staff Regulations and Rules, Financial Rules and Regulations, Code of Ethics and Conduct, Whistleblower Protection Policy, Information and Records Management policies, and other applicable governance frameworks.

PEDIDO DE MANIFESTAÇÕES DE INTERESSE

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA – CONSULTOR INDIVIDUAL)

 

PAÍS: São Tomé e Príncipe

Nome do Projeto: Segundo Projeto de Desenvolvimento do Setor dos Transportes e Resiliência

N.º do Empréstimo/ N.º do Crédito: IDA-V5210

Descrição: Contratação de um (a) coordenador (a) do projeto

Referência N.º 24/C/STCP/2026

 

O Governo de São Tomé e Príncipe (GoSTP) recebeu um Donativo da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA) para cobrir o custo do Segundo Projeto de Desenvolvimento do Setor dos Transportes e Resiliência e pretende aplicar uma parte desse donativo em serviços de consultoria para recrutamento de um (a) Coordenador para gerir a Unidade de Implementação do referido Projeto.

O objetivo deste recrutamento prende-se com os seguintes aspetos:

  • Assegurar a UIP na coordenação e planeamento das atividades do Projeto, garantindo a coerência entre os objetivos técnicos, os cronogramas de execução, os contratos de obras e de consultoria e os recursos disponíveis;
  • Acompanhar implementação técnica das atividades relacionadas com infraestruturas de transporte e proteção costeira, em articulação com o Instituto Nacional de Estradas (INAE), a Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP);
  • Contribuir para a monitorização global do desempenho do Projeto, incluindo o progresso físico e financeiro, apoiando a preparação de relatórios de progresso e a tomada de decisões informadas pela UIP e pelas entidades de tutela;

Assim sendo, a AFAP convida os consultores qualificados a formalizar candidaturas, anexando uma Carta de Intenção dirigida ao Diretor Geral da AFAP, Curriculum Vitae, Cópia do B.I, e dos comprovativos das formações e experiência de profissional descritas no curriculum vitae.

O(A) Coordenador (a) terá as seguintes tarefas e responsabilidades:

  • Preparar os planos e a programação anual das atividades e tarefas do Projeto, sua orçamentação e implementação atempada, em colaboração com as equipas do projeto;
  • Trabalhar em conjunto com as equipas do projeto, aconselhamento, elaboração dos termos de referência e outros documentos necessários para execução do projeto;
  • Coordenar e acompanhar a convocação das reuniões dos comités de pilotagem e dos comités técnicos do projeto, garantindo que as atas sejam preparadas e devidamente arquivadas;
  • Preparar os encontros mensais com a equipa do projeto, e outras partes interessadas, e elaborar as respetivas atas e relatórios;
  • Liderar a monitorização dos indicadores do Projeto, produzir Relatórios semestrais e anuais das atividades do progresso do projeto requeridos pelos financiadores, nomeadamente o Bando Mundial e o Fundo Global para o Ambiente (GEF);
  • Interagir com a AFAP para a boa e atempada realização dos processos de pagamento, aquisições, seguimento financeiro do projeto, o progresso da taxa de desembolso;
  • Assessorar e participar ativamente nas reuniões tecnicas de avaliação e missões de supervisão do Banco Mundial.

Os critérios de seleção do (a) Coordenador (a) do Segundo Projeto de Desenvolvimento do Setor dos Transportes e Resiliência são os seguintes:

  • Licenciatura em engenharia civil ou áreas afins (graduação de mestrado ou doutoramento seria uma vantagem);
  • Pelo menos 15 anos de experiência profissional;
  • Pelo menos 10 anos de experiência específica no sector de infraestruturas rodoviárias, incluindo planeamento, projeto, construção e/ou reabilitação de estradas, pontes, obras de arte, drenagem e demais estruturas associadas;
  • Experiência comprovada em gestão de contratos de empreitada de obras publicas, incluindo supervisão técnica, controlo de qualidade, gestão de prazos e custos, bem como capacidade de resolução de litígios contratuais e gestão de reclamações e sinistros;
  • Experiência em projetos financiados por Banco Mundial, com domínio das respetivas normas e procedimentos de procurement, gestão fiduciária, salvaguardas ambientais e sociais, preferencialmente com experiência como coordenador de projetos;
  • Elevada capacidade de comunicação, negociação e relacionamento interpessoal, bem como aptidão para trabalho em equipa multidisciplinar;
  • Fluência em língua portuguesa, ao nível da escrita, leitura, compreensão e expressão oral;
  • Domínio de pelo menos uma língua estrangeira, preferencialmente inglês, nas vertentes de escrita, leitura, compreensão e expressão oral.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Secção III, parágrafos, 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários do IPF" do Banco Mundial, setembro 2025 ("Regulamento de Aquisições"), que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial em matéria de conflito de interesses.

Os consultores interessados podem obter o Termo de Referência através do endereço electrónico: ptpc.procurement@afap.st e dg.procurement@afap.st

As manifestações de interesse devem ser entregues nas instalações da AFAP, no 2.º Andar, ou enviadas para o endereço eletrónico ptpc.procurement@afap.st e dg.procurement@afap.st até às 16h:00 (hora local) do dia 24/06/2026, devendo mencionar a referência e o nome do concurso.

Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos, São Tomé 12 de junho de 2026.

procnotices.project_name: Building Institutions And Systems to Harness And Realize Agenda 2063 Project
procnotices.bid_description: Consulting Service for the Development of the Dispute Settlement Portal - Firm Selection
procnotices.contact_address: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)   

Name of Project:                   Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063

Contract Title:                      Consulting Services for Developing Dispute Settlement Portal

Method of Selection:            Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) – International

Type of Contract:                 Lump-Sum Contract

 

Project ID:                             180117

Grant No.:                             E2020

Reference No.:                      ET-AFCFTA-541891-CS-CQS

 

  • The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

  • The consulting services (“the Services”) is for Developing the Dispute Settlement Portal. The firm will be responsible for developing the Dispute Settlement Portal. The primary deliverable of this consultancy will be the design, development, deployment and integration of a Dispute Settlement Portal into the existing AfCFTA website, to provide secure, structured public and administrative access to the Dispute Settlement Mechanism's institutional framework, processes, legal instruments and case information.

 

  • The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment found at the following website: https://au-afcfta.org/bids/ (home page).

 

  • The AfCFTA Secretariat now invites eligible interested firms to indicate their interests in providing the Services. Interested firms should provide information, as stipulated in the TOR, demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The consultant must meet the minimum qualification and selection criteria indicated below:

 

    1. A detailed Expression of Interest (EOI) clearly indicating the firms’ core business in CT/web-portal/workflow/case-management systems, minimum 5 years' experience (per TOR Section 10), registration, and relevant certifications (ISO 27001, cloud-platform cert) where held. (20%)
    2. Evidence of consultant’s experience in similar assignments with at least three (3) similar assignments on web-based portal, application development, workflow, or case/document-management systems, preferably for government/IGO/international-organization clients with signed, verifiable client references and evidence of satisfactory completion of the same assignments. (25%)
    3. An Expression of Interest (EOI) with a brief commentary on the TOR showing understanding of the Portal's modules, integration requirements, and the cloud-hosting task. Explicitly not a technical proposal, workplan, or methodology document. (15%)
    4. Proposed study team (Project Manager, Business Process Analyst, Designer & Developer, Trainer, Infrastructure/Cloud Deployment Expert, Legal and Dispute Settlement Expert) as per the TOR requirements, their qualifications and experience in undertaking the assignment plus copies of certificates and recommendations. (40%)

 

  • The Consultant(s) will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016 and revised 7th Edition of September 2025 which can be found at the following website: www.worldbank.org/procurement.

 

  • The duration of the consultancy services is Twelve (12) months.

 

  • The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition of September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

  • The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  • Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours [weekdays Monday to Friday 0800hrs to 1700hrs local time excluding public holidays]. Interested Consultants are required to constantly and continually check the AfCFTA website: https://au-afcfta.org/bids/ for any additional information or clarification that may arise before the submission date.

 

The Secretary General

The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat, Africa Trade House,

Ambassadorial Enclave, Liberia Road, Ridge, Accra, Ghana

Email address: Tender.AfCFTA@au-afcfta.org

Website: www.au-afcfta.org

 

  • Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address above (in person, or by e-mail) by 7th August, 2026 at 5.00 pm GMT.

procnotices.notice_text:
FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF SOMALIA

The Ministry of Finance

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

Country:

Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

Name of the Project:

Somalia Productive, Resilient and Inclusive Growth Project (SPRING),

Assignment Title:

Consultancy service to conduct Strategic Plan for National Payment System (NPS) – Somalia

Project ID:

P501662

Deadline for submission

 of EOI

8th August 2026 4:00pm

Individual/Firm:

firm Selection

Ref No.                                 SO-MOF-543502-CS-QCBS

 1. Background: In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance.

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.

The MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity, MoF intends to apply part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the Consultancy Service to conduct Strategic Plan National Payment System (NPS) – Somalia. (firm)

2. Responsibilities: The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified consulting firm (“Consultant”) to Develop a five-year strategic roadmap for modernizing Somalia’s NPS.: Strengthen DPI to enhance interoperability, accessibility, inclusiveness, and resilience: Align the NPS with BIS PFMIs, ISO 20022, and other global benchmarks: Support regional integration through harmonization with EAC and other frameworks: Incorporate innovations such as instant payments, open APIs, digital identity, and advanced risk management: Improve safety, efficiency, and robustness of the payment ecosystem: Provide actionable recommendations on governance, risk management, operations, and regulatory compliance. All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link:  https://centralbank.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/TOR_NPS_Strategic_Roadmap_Consultant_Firm_Somalia-1.pdf

3. Duration: The firm is expected to complete the proposed assignment within 12 Months.

4. The Ministry of Finance invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.). The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • I. Core business of the firm at least 10 years' experience in payment systems, financial sector reforms, or Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).
  • II. Specific experience in successfully implementing similar assignments. (Proven track record of previous similar experiences of successfully completing at least one (preferably two) assignment involving the development of National Payment System strategies, payment system modernization roadmaps, or similar financial market infrastructure strategies for central banks, financial regulators, or equivalent institutions) Proven expertise in BIS PFMIs, ISO 20022, instant payments, interoperability, financial inclusion, cybersecurity, and payment system governance. The Consultant shall provide the name and contact address of the Client (office and e-mail address and telephone number), date(s) of execution, name (s) of lead and associate firms, contract amount, and financing sources.
  • III. Experience of relevant services in an environment similar to that of Somalia and
  • IV. Technical and managerial organization of the firm (provide only the structure of the organization). Do not provide CVs of key staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.
  •  
  • 5.  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated in September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.   
  •  6.  Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected
  • 7.  A Consultant will be selected under the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. 
  • 8. Interested Consultants may obtain further information (in person or by e-mail) at the address below during office hours from 8.00 a.m. - 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday except on public holidays.
  • 9. Deadline for submission: Expressions of interest should be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 8th August 2026 4:00pm

Attention; Project Coordinator

Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project (VARS)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Individual Selection of Consultant

Country:

Government of Vanuatu

Name of the Project:

Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project

Assignment Title:

MoLNR Website Development Services

Individual/Firm:

Firm

Duty Station:

PMU, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources,

Port Vila, Vanuatu

Date of Publication:

20th July 2026

Deadline for submission:

3rd August 2026 at time: 1400 Hours (Vanuatu Time)

Reference Number:

VU-MLNR-551851-CS-CQS

1.         BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT:

A long-term vision of the Government of Vanuatu (GoV) is to provide potable water, sanitation, roads, drainage, and electricity to low-income households for the largest number of citizens.  To address this, the International Development Agency of the World Bank Group is supporting the GoV with the Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project (VARS).  Aims of the Project include developing a phased, 10-year, risk-informed Land Development, and Investment Strategy (LDIS) for the Greater Port Vila area with an estimated population of 114,000 people, almost 40 percent of the country’s population.  VARS also will support the GoV to prepare a five-year action plan to implement phased settlement upgrading (SURP) of the 23 existing informal settlements in the Greater Port Vila area.  To build towards these two interdependent medium-term platforms, the Project will implement on-the ground selected investments and associated institutional, and policy strengthening measures to pilot and set policy precedents for new land development and in situ settlement upgrading. This includes: (a) basic area upgrading of four informal settlements (Ohlen Mataso, Seaside, Tokyo and portion of Anamburu); (b) developing a 10 ha ‘sites-and-services’ (greenfield) lower-middle income residential area subdivision; (c) expansion or rehabilitation (as required) of off-site infrastructure focusing on flood management and mitigation; and (d) implementing measures for transformative institutional capacity strengthening of responsible Government of Vanuatu and sub-national agencies for planning, financing, and implementing the 10-year LDIS and 5-year SURP in partnerships with communities and the private sector.

2. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

2.1 General Objective

To design, develop, and deploy a secure, scalable, and user-friendly website for the Ministry of Lands based on the VFSC website model.

2.2 Specific Objectives

  • Provide access to land services and application forms online.
  • Improve transparency in land administration.
  • Publish laws, policies, directions, and procedures.
  • Enable public engagement and information dissemination.

4. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

The Consultant/Firm should possess:

  • Demonstrated competency and provide examples of previous experience in the performance of similar services.
  • At least 5 years of prior experience designing visually appealing and navigation friendly web sites.
  • Broad knowledge of current web development technologies and design tools in the field, and new software and other web programming languages and programs
  • Have excellent knowledge of recent trends in graphic design, web sites, including online video publishing, and social media networking; e) Demonstrate the ability to create innovative and visually appealing design.

The key expert deemed required to perform these services should possess:

  • Degree in Computer Science, IT, or related field
  • Minimum 5–10 years of experience in web development
  • Strong experience in CMS platforms and web technologies
  • Experience with GIS systems (QGIS, GeoNode, Leaflet, OpenLayers)
  • Experience in database development and integration
  • Knowledge of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, Python, and related technologies
  • Experience in developing government or large-scale platforms.
  • Experience in digital services and payment integration (desirable)
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
  • Familiarity with land information systems is an advantage.
  • Fluency in English

5. REPORTING:

  • Provide weekly progress updates to the IT Manager and Project Manager
  • Report on milestones, risks, and issues encountered.
  • Assist in preparation of documentation and training materials.

6. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT:

  • 12 Weeks

7. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS:

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017 August 2018, and November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Quality Selection (CQS) Method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Ministry in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 8.00 a.m.– 5.00 p.m. Monday to Friday.

Deadline: Expressions of interest and CV must be delivered to the address below by hand, mail, or email on or before 3rd August 2026 at 14:00 Hours Vanuatu Time.

THE UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE

REGIONAL ADMINISTRATION AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT

 

DAR ES SALAAM METROPOLITAN DEVELOPMENT PROJECT - PHASE 2 (DMDP 2)

IDA CREDIT NO. 7478-TZ

 

TENDER NO. ME56/WB-DMDPII/P180298/2025/2026/C/05                                                                

FOR

PROVISION OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR REVIEW, UPDATING OF DESIGNS, PREPARATION OF DETAILED ENGINEERING DESIGNS, TENDER DOCUMENTATION, AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF PRIORITY DRAINAGE INTERVENTIONS IN DAR ES SALAAM UNDER DMDP 2

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

1. This request for expressions of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for the Dar es Salaam Metropolitan Development Project - Phase 2 (DMDP 2) that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) online Notice No. OP00277705 of March 6, 2024.

2. The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Dar es Salaam Metropolitan Development Project – Phase 2 (DMDP 2), implemented by the Prime Minister’s Office – Regional Administration and Local Government (PMO-RALG) in collaboration with the Dar es Salaam Local Authorities. Part of the proceeds of this financing will be applied to eligible payments under the contract for the Provision of Consultancy Services for Review, Updating of Designs, Preparation of Detailed Engineering Designs, Tender Documentation, and Construction Supervision of Priority Drainage Interventions in Dar es Salaam under DMDP 2.

3. The overall objective of the assignment is to support PMO-RALG and the Dar es Salaam Local Authorities in reducing flood risk in priority catchments of Dar es Salaam by reviewing, refining, and delivering implementation-ready detailed engineering designs, tender documentation, procurement support, construction supervision, defects liability support, and operation and maintenance capacity building for selected priority drainage interventions under DMDP 2 Component 1.

4. The specific objectives of this assignment are to: (i) verify and evaluate the Strategic Priority Drainage Systems through rapid field investigations, hydraulic assessments, and stakeholder consultations; (ii) confirm a final list of priority drainage subprojects for detailed design within the available civil works investment envelope; (iii) update and refine priority intervention concepts to reflect current site conditions, completed DMDP 1 works, recent infrastructure developments, Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS), and climate resilience requirements; (iv) prepare detailed engineering designs, cost estimates, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities, and tender-ready documentation in accordance with applicable Tanzanian standards and good international engineering practice; (v) support procurement of works contractors, including technical inputs, responses to bidder queries, bid evaluation support, and contract award assistance; (vi) supervise construction of approved drainage works and administer works contracts to ensure compliance with approved designs, specifications, contractual obligations, and environmental and social safeguard requirements; (vii) support the Defects Liability Period through inspections, certification of rectification of defects, final accounts, and completion documentation; and (viii) strengthen institutional capacity of the Dar es Salaam Local Authorities (LGAs) through Operation and Maintenance plans, manuals, funding assessment, and targeted training of LGA technical staff.

5. The assignment will be implemented in two phases, the first phase being the design phase, followed by a brief period to allow for procurement of works contractors and the second phase being for construction supervision, contract management, defects liability period monitoring and contract completion. and will comprise: (i) inception, review of existing studies and data, site verification, preliminary engineering investigations, design basis confirmation, and evaluation of alternatives for the nine (9) Strategic Priority Drainage Systems; (ii) preparation of detailed engineering designs and complete tender documentation for the Client-approved; (iii) procurement support to the Client, including technical clarifications, pre-bid support, bid evaluation inputs, and contract award assistance; and (iv) full construction supervision and contract administration, followed by support during the twelve (12) month Defects Liability Period (DLP). The consultancy will focus on the Strategic Priority Drainage Systems identified in the TOR, with the final package for detailed design and implementation to be confirmed through Stage 1 engineering analysis, stakeholder validation, safeguards considerations, and the available investment envelope.

6. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: https://www.tamisemi.go.tz. Requests for clarification should be sent through the following e-mail addresses: cities.project@yahoo.com or cities.project@tamisemi.go.tz, and the Client will send responses to clarifications through the same e-mail addresses.

7. The Permanent Secretary, PMO-RALG, now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the above services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The short-listing criteria are: (a) Type of core business and at least 10 years in relevant business; (b) Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the following: (i) Experience in similar assignments - information to be provided should include the name of the assignments, the names and full contact addresses of the clients, the contract value (in equivalent US dollars), the period (month/year) of execution of the assignments, and the role played in the assignments (Lead or JV Partner); (ii) Demonstration of experience working in similar conditions; and (c) The firm's technical and managerial capability (provide only the organizational structure, and the general qualifications, field of expertise and number of key personnel). Do not provide the CVs of the staff. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but they should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) and/or a Sub-Consultant. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Therefore, each member of the JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria. The experience, technical & managerial capability of the sub-consultant shall not be evaluated to enhance the qualification of the Lead Firm or JV. Consultants shall not use the Affiliate Member's Managerial, Technical or Experience Capabilities to enhance their qualifications.

Note that: The Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) for this Consultancy Services for Review, Updating of Designs, Preparation of Detailed Engineering Designs, Tender Documentation, and Construction Supervision of Priority Drainage Interventions in Dar es Salaam under the DMDP 2 is being advertised at the same time together with the other two (2) Tenders for Consultancy Services for: (i) Design and Construction Supervision of Area-Based Investments and Urban Infrastructure in Kinondoni and Ubungo Municipalities under the DMDP 2, and (ii) Design and Construction Supervision of Area-based Investments and Urban Infrastructure in Dar es Salaam City, Temeke Municipality and Kigamboni Municipality; and the assignments in these three Tenders will be executed simultaneously. Hence, in order for a firm shortlisted in two or three tenders to be contracted for Consultancy Services in either two or three tenders; it must propose separate Key Experts for each Tender in both Technical and Financial Proposals.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

10. Expression of Interest marked: “EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR THE PROVISION OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR REVIEW, UPDATING OF DESIGNS, PREPARATION OF DETAILED ENGINEERING DESIGNS, TENDER DOCUMENTATION, AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF PRIORITY DRAINAGE INTERVENTIONS IN DAR ES SALAAM UNDER DMDP 2” should be delivered in a written form to the Secretary, Ministerial Tender Board, Prime Minister’s Office, Regional Administration and Local Government (PMO-RALG), CDA Road, Sokoine House, Wing A, Second Floor, Office of the Procurement Management Unit (PMU), Room No. 133, P.O.
